result.description: Fires on varied tokens (" the", verbs like "seeks to", "involves") inside the predicate of a definitional sentence about a field or discipline ("X is a complex field that ..."). Silent on " the" in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Field-definition sentence predicate

result.description: Fires mainly on ' a' in "without leaving a remainder" in definitions of the greatest common divisor, and weakly on related words like "without" and "of". It stays silent on ' a' in other sentences.
result.label: "leaving a remainder" article

result.description: Fires on the period ending a short title-like list item (e.g. "Dough Folding.") in lists of topic headings, where the next line repeats the same head word. It stays quiet on single-word or unrelated-topic list items.
result.label: Period after repeated-topic list heading

result.description: Fires on subject pronouns or verbs (' we', ' they', ' express', ' learned', ' is') right after "what/how" in embedded clauses like "how we express ourselves" or "what we say". Silent on 'we' in ordinary main clauses. Weak, mixed circuit.

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied function words and word pieces (to, in, and, that, 's) in technical or engineering-style text. Predicts process-like words (processing, manip, communication). The circuit failed and the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens in abstract expository prose: commas, ' of', closing parens, word-piece endings, where a noun or clause continuation follows. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak (failed faithfulness); no clear single trigger.
result.label: Scattered punctuation/function tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, most often a possessive apostrophe after a plural noun (vessels') but also ' have', ' while', 'atile'. It is silent on contraction apostrophes and singular possessives. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Plural possessive apostrophe, mixed

result.description: Fires mostly on ' quickly' right after a subject noun like "the approach" (before a verb such as spread), with weaker hits on ' since', commas and ' to'. Members are diffuse generic context latents; the circuit is weak and mixed.

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on varied words (changing, a, their, social) inside grammar-essay text about tenses and sentence structure. Members are grammar-term detectors (plural, clause, subject). Evidence is thin and inconsistent.

result.description: Fires on function words or verbs (' or', ' for', ',', ' provide', 'offers') shortly after the word "pause" in text about pauses and silence. The same words stay silent in other contexts, such as "conflicts or dissatisfaction".

result.description: Weak, scattered attention-layer target peaking on mixed tokens ('that', ' the', a space, 'etic') in genetics/explanatory text. Members are generic token detectors with no discriminative ingredients; the circuit failed and the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function-word peaks, unclear

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' to' after "designed", also 'can', 'of', 'they') in aerospace/spacecraft engineering text. It is silent on many identical ' to' tokens, and the evidence does not show what separates them.

result.description: Scattered peaks on 'ing', commas, ' task', ' and' and other mid-sentence words in abstract expository text. The same 'ing' in 'analyzing' fires in some contexts and not others. Members are generic and non-discriminative, so the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (' intellig', ' network', 'ven', ' other') that follow "and"/"or" in coordinated lists of technical terms. Peaks are inconsistent, and the target is silent on ' intellig' in some contexts. The evidence is weak and mixed.

result.description: Fires on commas and "or" inside a list of items (e.g. "stringed, brass or", "cost structures, affordability"), where another list item is expected next. Silent on commas that follow clauses. Evidence is weak and the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires on varied function words and nouns (with, providing, of, experiences, and) in text about social media and technology platforms giving users or artists something. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is diffuse, so the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on ' countries' (also 'nations', ' to', ' and') as the subject right after "as" in a fiscal-policy clause ("as countries grappled with..."). Silent on 'countries' after "many" or "in". Weak, low-faithfulness circuit.

Fires on commas, "and", "the", "as" within lists of metrics or evaluation concepts (reach, cost, recall, precision), where another list item or measure is expected. Silent on commas in other marketing prose. Weak circuit evidence.

result.description: Fires on modal or copular verbs (' can', ' are', ' may', ' all') right after a plural subject noun, especially "factors" (e.g. "factors can influence"). Members are mostly "factors" detectors. Contrast shows silence after other plural subjects; the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and nouns (' to', ' more', ' and', ' stories', "'s") right after a plural agent noun like geographers, writers, chefs or artists in academic or creative-writing text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires on a word right after "mathematical"/academic-type adjectives (e.g. "mathematical and", "mathematical thought", "reasoning"), the slot where a noun or coordinated adjective follows in abstract academic prose. Silent on other " and" uses. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' cla' when it begins "clauses" in grammar text, usually after a modifier like independent, main, relative or dependent. Weaker on "claws"; silent in a non-grammar use of "clauses".

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' and', ' which', word suffixes, 's, ' by') in abstract academic-style prose, mid-phrase. Peaks are mixed with no shared token or construction; the circuit looks diffuse and failed near threshold.

The same ' and' stays silent in similar sentences, so the trigger is diffuse and the circuit's faithfulness is poor.

result.description: Fires on function words (' are', ' the', ' by', ' as', ' of') right after the subject in glacial-striation text, where a predicate or description follows. Silent on 'are' in other glacier or landform sentences, so it is selective.

result.description: Fires on 'ough' in "dough" and on function words (of, in, a) in text about dough, bread and baking. Silent on 'ough' in other positions such as sourdough or mid-sentence. Members are mostly dough detectors with some cooking-topic members.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and commas (the, an, in, and, ',') in expository academic-style text, mid-phrase where a noun or list item comes next. Contrast shows commas staying silent in other positions. Evidence is mixed and weak.

result.description: Fires on function words like "various", "different", "of", "within" right after "networks/integration of" in definitional text about innovation ecosystems, just before a list of entities or institutions. Silent on "of" after other nouns elsewhere.

result.description: Fires on ' of' (rarely ' the') in the opening sentence of a document, after an abstract noun like "narrative", "context" or "symphony". It stays silent on ' of' after "period of" or "era of" in historical text. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the '9' in a year like 1914/1918/1945, mostly the second year of a range ("from 1914 to 1918") or a year in a war-era context. It stays quiet on '9' in decade forms like "1920s" or in other years.

result.description: Fires on 'on' (and 'hole') in the split word "Pigeonhole" in "Pigeonhole Principle". Members detect the preceding word pieces 'P', 'ige', 'hole'. Silent on 'on' in other words like "Fibonacci".

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (word endings like 'ed', ' while', ' visual', ' and') inside text about painting and visual art styles. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit failed and members mostly carry art context.

result.description: Fires on 'ding' in "nodding" and on tokens right after "nodding" or "nod" (gently, and, 's) in text about non-verbal communication and active listening. Members detect nod, eye contact, listening and gesture words.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (word pieces like 'itive', periods, ' to', ' and', ' data') in expository or academic prose. No consistent token or context; the circuit failed faithfulness and members are generic.

result.description: Fires mostly on the document-start token, plus occasional odd tokens like ' structure' or a hyphen. Silent on many document-start tokens in the contrast. Members are scattered token detectors, so the evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.

result.description: Mixed peaks: mostly ' E' in Einstein's "E=mc2", plus scattered commas and function words. Silent on other "E=mc2" contexts, so the condition is unclear. Members are generic word-piece detectors; the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' fourth', ' pl', ' of', ' elect', function words) inside text about plasma physics, where it seems to predict plasma/fusion-related continuations like 'asma' and 'charge'. Members are plasma/tokamak/fusion detectors. Mixed token peaks.

result.description: Fires on function words (by, of, the, that) and title pieces in the opening of expository academic text, especially around the Universal Law of Gravitation. It is silent on the same words elsewhere, so the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the end of a noun or suffix piece (phrasing, -ism, frescoes, markets, sequences) that follows "from X to the [adjective] ..." in a list of cultural or artistic examples. Peak tokens vary; the logits are unclear.

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on hyphens, ' and', ' that', ' could' and mid-word pieces in expository text. Hyphens fire in some places but stay silent in others (event-based, risk-free). Members are generic token detectors; the circuit failed.

result.description: Fires on scattered connector or punctuation tokens (and, or, from, where, comma) early in a document, often where an alias or appositive follows (Forex or FX, educator and psychologist). Peaks are inconsistent and the evidence is weak.

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on 's' after Chaucer's possessive and sometimes 'The' or 'other' in literary-history text about Chaucer. It stays silent on 'The' inside quoted titles. Circuit failed, with diffuse members.

result.description: Diffuse, low-consistency target peaking on assorted tokens (party, comma, hyphen, 'ing', mid-word pieces, subject nouns/verbs) in expository text. Members are generic token and word-piece detectors; no clear shared trigger or condition. Circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires on function words and punctuation (' a', ' an', ' the', commas, 'is') right after a music-technique term being defined or listed, such as vibrato, staccato, legato. Silent on ' a' in general musical prose.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' to', ' in', ' of', ' are') and word pieces in abstract expository text on math, philosophy and history. The peak token varies and the same tokens often stay silent elsewhere. Evidence is mixed and weak.

result.description: Fires on ' be' right after the modal "can" (also "cannot"), where a passive participle comes next (classified, likened, seen). Silent in some contexts with the same "can be" in non-verbal communication or culinary text, so the extra condition is unclear.

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (a suffix piece, a digit, commas, ' a', ' invest') in expository text. No dominant token or condition is visible, and the circuit failed faithfulness, so this is a weak, mixed target.

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", "through" and some nouns inside lists or enumerations of items, where the next element continues a series. Silent on many commas in ordinary prose. Weak, failed circuit with mixed evidence.

result.description: Fires on commas and function words (and, to, the) that follow a list item or noun phrase in abstract expository text, where another item or continuation is expected. Mixed peaks, weak circuit, and silent on similar commas in the contrast.

result.description: Fires on prepositions (of, in, to, between, as) following abstract nouns like "components", "roles", "operation" near the start of expository documents about input/peripheral devices. Silent on similar "of" in other electronics text, so the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the space token before a number (century or year like "800", "7th") in texts about ancient traditions and history, such as Vedic works dated "around 800". Silent on some similar spaces before numbers, so the condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on function words (' a', ' the', ' to', ' of') right after a document-opening subject like "Transduction," or "Transduction is", in definitional openings. Stays silent on the same words in mid-text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is unfaithful.

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (aking, who, promoted, of, 9) in text about Nikola Tesla, shortly after his name. Likely carries "Tesla" context forward to predict Tesla-related continuations. Silent on 'T' as a unit or abbreviation.

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function tokens (commas, 'the', 'or', ')', 'by') mid-sentence, often in lists or after a listed item. The evidence is mixed: it is silent on many commas, and the circuit fails faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly ' the', also ' and', commas, 's) in physics text about speed/velocity, shortly after the word "speed". Silent on ' the' in other physics contexts such as sound or frequency. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.

result.description: Weak, scattered target firing on mixed tokens ('ential', ' course', ' the', ' (', ' and') in technical or science-explanation text. Members are generic and non-discriminative, so no clear trigger or condition emerges. The circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires mostly on ' and' (also ' as', ' to', ' all') joining items in lists of techniques or methods, e.g. "laser cleaning and X-ray". Silent on many other ' and' uses. Circuit is weak and diffuse; the condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (it, comma, in, their, allow, 's) mid-sentence in academic or expository text, where the next word is a content word. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires on varied function tokens (commas in lists of techniques, ' be', ' and', ')') in expository lists and hedged phrasing; the contrast shows the same commas often stay silent, and the evidence is mixed and weak.

result.description: Fires mostly on ' fost' (as in fostering/fosters) in abstract expository prose, plus occasional verb-like slots (provide, encompasses, ensures) where a transitive verb is expected. Silent on some ' fost' cases, so the extra condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (' and', ',', ' for', ' as', ' they', ' reproduce') in abstract expository prose, mid-clause where a coordinated or continuing item follows. Silent on 'and' in plain lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.

result.description: Fires on digits within year numbers (e.g. 1857, 1200 CE) and some function words in history-of-ideas text about India or ancient cultures. Silent on '0' in decade forms like 1980s or 1900. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.

result.description: Fires on function words (the, which, that, where, by) following mentions of non-Mendelian genetics or inheritance, in genetics passages. Silent on 'the' in other contexts. Members are mostly genetics/DNA-related detectors.

result.description: Fires on scattered function tokens ('s, the, of, commas, verb endings) in abstract academic or expository prose, mid-phrase before a noun. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, with no clear trigger or condition.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (and, the, commas, are, having) in expository academic prose, mid-list or mid-phrase where a noun or continuation is expected. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak; peaks are inconsistent.

result.description: Fires on varied tokens inside list-like enumerations (e.g. acronym lists such as HIPAA, FDA, EMA, and; separators like '/' and ','; word starts like ' di'), where another list item is expected. Weak, mixed circuit that failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires on function words in "both X and Y" / "either heads or tails" style constructions, where a pair of alternatives is being set up (e.g. "both the body part and", "resulting in either"). Evidence is weak and mixed; the circuit failed faithfulness.

result.description: Fires on ' understanding' (also analysis, grasp, explanation, knowledge) as a noun right after an adjective like thorough, deep, clear, nuanced. Silent when 'understanding' is a verb or follows 'for'/'mutual' or starts a clause.

result.description: Fires on the verb "follow" / "following" (and variants) when used as "obey or adhere to" (following steps, rules, practices), often after "by" or "to". Members are detectors of follow/following tokens.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: 'b' as a word-start piece (herb, hebdomad), ' flag', 'st', and function words like 'that', 'for', 'with'. Peaks are inconsistent. Logits favor word-continuation pieces. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on data-like nouns (' data', ' image', ' text', ' values') when they are the object of a processing verb such as organizing, normalizing or transforming, in machine-learning and preprocessing text. It stays silent on ' data' as a subject or after "the" or adjectives.

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' care', ' knowledge', ' services', 'V', mid-word pieces like 'sur', 'dis') in abstract or technical prose. No single token dominates; peaks look like word-internal or noun slots. Evidence is mixed and the circuit's faithfulness is poor.

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'light' (sunlight, lighting) and a few other tokens like ' delay', ' electric', ' bass' in descriptive text on music, sound or light. Silent on 'light' in 'spotlight'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is a weak fit.

result.description: Fires on "transition" (and variants like "itions") and related change-of-state words such as "switch", mostly describing a shift from one state to another, often in physical or material science contexts. Predicts "from/between" style continuations.

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (commas, "becomes", "initially", "signals", "range") that come right after a subject in explanatory passages about stages or processes, such as language development. Silent on commas in statistics text. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on mixed function words and adverbs (" the", " is", "essentially", "-ically", country names) in expository text, often after "of", "constitute", "regarded as", where a word like "same" or "essential" may follow. Silent on " the" after "of" in math contexts. Evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces that need a continuation to form a compound or word, mainly ' back' (backbone, backups) and 'ru' in 'disruptions'. It predicts a suffix piece like 'bone' or 'drop'. Silent on 'back' in 'backpropagation'.

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' cot' (as in cotton) when it comes mid-text, expecting a continuation like 'ton'. Silent when ' cot' is the first token of the document. Members detect similar incomplete word-start pieces (nit, foss, fab, fi).

result.description: Fires mainly on " comes" in "when it comes to", and also on " Cir" at the start of a "Circles" heading. Weaker hits fall on mid-word pieces like "a" in Versailles. Mixed peaks, with a dominant "comes" family.

result.description: Fires on the word " recent", most strongly in "in recent years", with weaker firing on similar time adjectives like "subsequent", "respective", "contemporary". Predicts time nouns such as years, times, history.
result.label: " recent" in "in recent years"

result.description: Fires on ' one' used as a pronoun after "the" (e.g. "the one with/that/in"), a relative-clause head. It stays silent on ' one' as a bare subject, or as a numeral before a noun ("in one place").
result.label: "the one" pronoun after determiner

result.description: Fires on connective function words (through, with, of, and, or, from, whether) following a noun like "visionaries" or "influence" in essays about leaders and influential people, where a continuation specifying how or what kind is expected. Weak and inconsistent.
result.label: Connectives after visionaries/leaders in essays

result.description: Fires on varied words in decision/choice contexts (making, treated, chosen, choices, effective) that follow a possessive or subject and precede an object noun or complement. Peaks are scattered and the circuit evidence is diffuse.
result.label: Decision/choice words before complement

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ac' when it follows "language" and begins "acquisition" (language ac|quisition). It stays silent on ' ac' in other contexts such as "acquire" or a bare "acquisition" after "of".
result.label: "ac" in "language acquisition"

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces ('in', 'ced', 'ver', 'iv') inside longer words like pronominations, antecedents, vocabulary, in English-grammar text about pronouns and agreement. Likely predicts word-ending suffixes such as 'ent' or 'ant'.
result.label: Mid-word pieces in grammar terminology

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments like 'est' in "livestock" (also 'ol', 'ell'), where a word is split into pieces and the 'est' piece comes after a prefix. Silent when 'est' starts the text. Members detect 'est' in Aesthetic, Underestimation.
result.label: mid-word 'est' piece (livestock)

result.description: Fires on function words (' the', ' one', ' with', ' of', ' another') in the middle of noun phrases, often after a name or in lists and coordinations (e.g. "Catherine the", "and the Gupta"). Silent on many ' the' tokens elsewhere. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in coordinated noun phrases

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ' to', ' or', ' possible', 'ating', commas) in expository science and academic text, often where a list or coordinated item continues. Peaks are inconsistent and it is silent on many ' and' tokens.
result.label: Scattered connectives in expository text

result.description: Fires on the token ' sea' (also ' Sea'), strongest as the first piece of "seafood" and "SeaChoice", and more weakly in "sea level". Upstream members are sea/marine/ocean detectors. The word-start use in compounds seems to matter.
result.label: ' sea' as start of compounds

result.description: Fires on varied mid-word pieces like 'od', 'ous', 'ate' and some function words, mostly in linguistics or technical expository text. The 'od' detectors in the members (Geodetic, Kodak, melodies) feed it, but the peaks are scattered and consistency is low.
result.label: Scattered word-piece 'od'/'ous' in expository text

result.description: Fires on ' gen' (of genetics) and ' inheritance' when directly after "Mendelian". It stays silent on ' gen' after other words like "field of", "developmental", "into", so it needs the preceding word "Mendelian".
result.label: Mendelian genetics/inheritance

result.description: Fires on 'World' in 'post-World War II' (after the prefix 'post-'), anticipating 'War'. Members detect 'World'/'Cold' before 'War' and post-/prefix pieces; silent on unrelated text.
result.label: post-World (War II)

result.description: Fires on words in phrases about developing language or skill abilities (creative writing, communication skills, English, one's skills/ability), in educational self-improvement text. It is silent on some 'writing' tokens in other constructions, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Writing and communication skill phrases

result.description: Fires on ' is' (rarely ' are') in scientific text, mostly right after the relative pronoun "which" or after a comma-set-off noun phrase. It stays quiet on ' is' after "understanding X" gerund subjects.
result.label: ' is' after "which" in science text

result.description: Fires on the word " roots" (also "root", "ots") across senses: origins, word roots, math roots, plant roots. Members are mostly detectors of "roots"/"root" tokens. Silent on unrelated text.
result.label: ' roots' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on the degree sign '°' after a number in temperature or coordinate expressions (e.g. 2300°f, 80°F, 14°S). Occasional weak firing on ' River' and ' and'. Members are mostly '°' detectors plus number and separator detectors.
result.label: Degree sign after numbers

result.description: Fires on ' the' after a verb or preposition in mathematical or procedural explanations (replace the, where the, substituting the), where a specific previously mentioned item is expected. Silent on some ' the' in abstract or proof-style text.
result.label: ' the' after verb in math procedures

result.description: Fires on tokens within SMART-goal lists (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant), such as "urable", "ifiable", "levant" and "goals", in goal-setting and project-planning text. It stays silent on "measurable" in other goal contexts.
result.label: SMART goals criteria tokens

result.description: Fires on the digit '7' (occasionally '9') when it starts a number, such as at document start or a section number like "7.4", or in a leading digit slot. It stays silent on '7' in the middle of a year like 1750 or 1970s.
result.label: Digit 7 at number start
' Berlin' in Cold War context
result.description: Fires on the token ' Berlin', mainly in Cold War / post-WWII history (Berlin Blockade, Berlin Wall, divided Berlin). Members include Berlin detectors plus Soviet and Vienna detectors. Contrast text without the word stays silent.

Fires on a mid-word piece such as 'vent' or 'intent' inside longer words like unconventional, unintentional, interventions, where the word continues with an '-ional' or '-ions' suffix. Predicts the suffix 'ional'.
result.label: Mid-word 'vent' before -ional

result.description: Fires on ' variety' as the head noun in "a variety of" (also weakly "an array of"), after an article. Silent when 'variety' is a bare noun, as in "soft-hair variety" or "celebrate variety in".
result.label: "a variety of" quantifier noun

result.description: Fires on the word " abstract" (as adjective, in art and concept contexts such as abstract form, abstract concepts, abstract art). Members are mostly detectors of "abstract" and related words like theoretical and objective.
result.label: ' abstract' token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'c' piece inside "vis-c-ous/viscosity" (fluid viscosity), and on similar mid-word pieces like 'ist' or 'ity'. Silent on 'c' in other words such as "molecule", so it needs the word 'viscous/viscosity'.
result.label: 'c' inside "viscous/viscosity"

result.description: Fires on ' of' (also ' for') right after "methods", "means", "techniques", where a gerund or process noun naturally follows (methods of shading, methods for determining). Silent on ' of' after "applications", "examples", "combinations".
result.label: 'of/for' after methods/techniques

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, mostly ' Plan' after Marshall and 'agan' in Reagan, in economic/policy text about government programs. Members mostly carry economy and policy themes. Evidence is mixed and only moderately consistent.
result.label: Economic-policy names (Marshall Plan, Reagan)

result.description: Fires mainly on the piece 'log' in the middle of a longer word (crystallography, phylogenetic, syllogism), where earlier word pieces like 'crystal' or 'phy' precede it. Occasionally fires on '2' in 'Level 2'.
result.label: 'log' inside multi-piece words

result.description: Fires on a full stop ending a sentence in academic or expository text about economics, geography and social topics. It is silent on many periods elsewhere, and the contrast does not show a clear difference.
result.label: Sentence-final period in academic economics text

result.description: Fires on the final piece of a statistical or epidemiological term, mainly 'isk' in "Attributable Risk", also 'io' in "Odds Ratio" and 'ence'. Appears in statistics and epidemiology text, completing multi-token terms.
result.label: Statistics term endings (Risk, Ratio)

result.description: Fires on the ending piece of a plural place-type noun (ecosystem-s, habit-ats, landsc-apes, areas) that is the object of "restore/restoring", right before "to their original/natural...". Silent on plural 's' elsewhere.
result.label: Plural ecosystem noun after restore

result.description: Fires on the 'bau' piece in 'Aufbau' and on assorted function words (in, the, new, through) in expository science or history passages. Peaks are mixed and the logits are unclear, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Aufbau 'bau' plus scattered function words

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece " rib" when it begins "ribosomal"/"ribosome" words, mostly in molecular biology text. Members are mostly detectors of " rib" and similar word-start fragments. Weak firing on a few other words.
result.label: word-initial "rib" of ribosomal

result.description: Fires on the word " smallest" (rarely " tiny"), usually after "the", as in "the smallest unit/possible". Upstream members detect smallest/largest/lowest/small/tiny/single-type size and extreme adjectives.
result.label: " smallest" superlative detector

result.description: Fires on varied words inside "strategies include..." style lists about efficiency and management (reduce, energy, managing, implementing), in engineering/operations text. Silent on some "reduce" tokens, so the exact requirement is unclear.
result.label: Efficiency/management strategy verbs

result.description: Fires mostly on " historical" as a modifier in lists of causes shaping culture or cuisine (e.g. "shaped by historical traditions"). Occasional weaker hits on other tokens. Members are mostly history/historical detectors plus factor-type words.
result.label: "historical" as causal modifier

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' of', ' and', ' population', 'lacement') in academic or expository lists and topic headings. No consistent token or context; the contrast shows ' of' often silent. Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (prepositions, word pieces like ' oppos', 'brace', ' Un') in expository academic or business text, mid-phrase before an abstract noun. Peaks are inconsistent; the logits favor abstract nouns such as elements, features and ideas. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens before abstract nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'am' inside "seamless/seamlessly" (also other 'am' pieces like "among", "contamination"), predicting a suffix like "lessly". Silent on other tokens.
result.label: 'am' in "seamless"

result.description: Fires on " but" after a "not limited to X" / "not just X" negated-scope clause, where "but also/rather" follows. It leans toward verbs like "encompasses/extends". Silent on other "not just... but" cases.
result.label: "but" in "not limited to X, but"

result.description: Fires on prepositions and verbs (of, into, in, to, shape, construct) that follow abstract academic nouns like "insights", "causes" or "trends", where a content noun phrase comes next. Silent on "of" right after a noun at document start. Members are mostly linguistics-topic detectors.
result.label: Academic abstract-noun connector words

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'mc' in E=mc², 'ord' in words like Chord/primordial, and ' Past' in 'Past Perfect'. Peaks are mixed word pieces with no shared meaning; the circuit evidence is weak and scattered.
result.label: Mixed word pieces: mc, ord, Past

result.description: Fires on the 'r' piece in "nut|r|ition" / "nut|r|itional" when mid-sentence (e.g. "enhance the nutrition of"). It stays silent on the same word at document start and on 'r' in carbohydrates.
result.label: 'r' inside nutrition

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, mostly hyphens (CRISPR-Cas9), commas, 'in' and ' defect', often in biology or science text. It is silent on many hyphens in compounds like child-rearing or fast-paced. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is only partly faithful.
result.label: Scattered hyphen and science-term firing

result.description: Fires on the word-piece "ient" completing "ingredient" (e.g. "key ingred-ient", "secret ingred-ient"). Members are mostly detectors of "ient" and "ients". It is weakly active on similar phrases such as "secret weapon".
result.label: "ient" in "ingredient"

result.description: Fires on the token ' cut' (also cuts, cutting) across both knife/food-cutting and reducing-costs uses. Members are mostly detectors of 'cut' and its word pieces. Predicts continuations like 'down', 'costs', 'outs'.
result.label: ' cut' token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on a leading ' -' at the very start of a document (list-like idiom entries such as "- Break the ice"), and on word pieces like 'mos' in "Atmospheric". Silent on ' -' after earlier text. Mixed, low-faithfulness circuit.
result.label: Document-initial dash and word pieces

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ation' completing the word "Communication", mostly in heading-like lists of communication types or channels. It stays silent on 'ation' in other words (orchestration, elaboration, punctuation) and in "Group Communication Theory".
result.label: 'ation' ending "Communication"

result.description: Fires on prepositions and weaving or metaphor words (' through', ' upon', ' by', ' threads') in abstract, figurative academic prose. It often sits where "which/whom" may follow, as in "through which" or "upon which". The peaks are mixed and fairly inconsistent.
result.label: Figurative 'through/upon which' prepositions

result.description: Fires on ' the' (also ' their', 'aping' in "shaping") after verbs/prepositions like "shaping", "crucial to", "imprint on", where an abstract object follows (economy, legacy, policies) in essays about influence. Silent on many other 'the' tokens.
result.label: the/their after shaping-influence verbs

result.description: Fires on scattered function or generic words (' you', ' way', ' one', ' this', ' By') in mid-phrase positions, where the next word is a noun-like completion (logits favour part/letter/body/sheet). The same ' you' stays silent in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words before noun

result.description: Fires on importance adjectives (crucial, essential, pivotal) in the predicate after "Understanding X is ...", right before "for/to/in". It stays quiet when "crucial" is used attributively (crucial tool, crucial roles, crucial insights).
result.label: Predicate "is crucial/essential" after understanding

result.description: Fires on word pieces that start a longer word, mainly " adjust" (before -ment) and " rou" (before -ters), plus a few odd tokens. Members are detectors of "adjust" and similar word-start pieces.
result.label: adjust / rou word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on the noun "impact" (also "impress-ions", "imprint") when it is a noun after adjectives like lasting, emotional or enduring. It stays silent on "impact" used as a verb ("will impact their work").
result.label: Noun 'impact'/'impressions' after lasting

result.description: Fires on the end of change-noun plurals like "advancements", "changes", "challenges" in the opening phrase of a document ("Despite the challenges...", "With the pace of technological advancements..."). Silent on the same token later in the text or when it opens the sentence.
result.label: Change/challenge plural in opening clause

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in science/academic list-like text: " Environment" at document start, "lication" in DNA replication, commas in lists. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Mixed academic-topic tokens, diffuse

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' and', ' of', ' in', ' during') and word pieces like ' Nak' inside lists or technical prose. Peaks are mixed, and ' and' is often silent in the contrast. The circuit is diffuse and its condition is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse function-word mid-phrase firing

result.description: Fires on scattered word-start fragments (' So' of "Soil" in topic lists, ' dimin', ' relev', 'form') where a longer word continues. Peaks are mixed, with no single token or topic dominating, and the evidence is weak.
result.label: Word-start fragments, mixed (So-il)

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", and nouns inside lists or coordinated pairs in expository text (pests and diseases, happiness, anger, surprise, flavor, texture, content). Peaks are mixed and consistency is low. The contrast gives no clear condition.
result.label: List items and commas in enumerations

result.description: Fires on connecting words (" in", "of", "ing", "with") right after a cooking-technique verb phrase such as "involves cooking food quickly in a small amount of...", where the next words describe the method's conditions. Silent on " in" in other food or general contexts.
result.label: Cooking method description connectors

result.description: Fires mostly on the word-start piece " nu" (as in "nuanced"), where the next piece is likely "anced"/"ance". It also fires weakly on scattered tokens such as " TCP" and commas. Silent on " nu" in "differing nuances".
result.label: ' nu' before 'anced' (nuance)

result.description: Fires on varied function words (" Now", " and", " to", " we", " or") at clause or list junctions in expository text, often where a new item or verb phrase is about to start. Peaks are inconsistent; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words at clause junctions

result.description: Fires on the word piece " tack" at the start of "tackle" (to tackle problems/challenges), as a verb-stem fragment before "-le". Members detect other word-start fragments that continue into verb suffixes like -le/-ling.
result.label: "tack" in "tackle"

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ver' inside words such as Adverbs, nonverbal, beverages and sovereign, where it is a non-final fragment. Weaker on Tversky and Lever. Silent in 'whichever'.
result.label: 'ver' word fragment (Ad-ver-bs)

result.description: Fires on scattered function or connecting words (' and', ' many', ' particularly', ' to') in expository text, where a content word or continuation is expected next. No dominant token, and it stays silent on many ' and' uses. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered connector words in expository text

result.description: Fires on comparative/superlative degree words (' more', ' most', ' less') right after a linking verb like "is/are/be", where an adjective or participle is expected next. Silent when 'more' directly modifies a noun or follows "even/of".
result.label: 'more/most' after linking verb

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'st' piece inside "crystallize/crystallization", where a word is split mid-way. It stays silent on 'st' in "workstations" and ordinal "21st". Other weak peaks are mid-word fragments.
result.label: 'st' in cry-st-allize

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' may', commas, ' to', ' s') in finance and economics text about futures, hedging, interest rates and price changes. Peak token varies; the shared theme is financial/economic context, and it is silent on ' may' in other topics.
result.label: Finance/economics text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on varied function words and suffixes (' of', ' offers', ' for', 'ized', ' behind') in blockchain/digital-technology text, mostly in early positions of documents. Silent on 'ized' in non-tech contexts like 'standardized' or 'specialized'.
result.label: Blockchain/tech text connective tokens

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (word pieces, commas, ' in') in abstract academic text on economics, strategy and optimization, mid-phrase. Peaks are scattered and the contrast shows the same comma silent, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in economics/strategy prose

result.description: Fires on past-tense contribution verbs (introduced, contributed, played, -ered, created) right after a named historical figure as subject, in text about intellectual or artistic history. Silent on passive "pioneered by".
result.label: Verbs of contribution after famous figures

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' the', ' of', ' a', 'ound') in abstract academic text about arts, culture and society, in mid-phrase positions. It stays silent on ' the' before period names such as Renaissance. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in abstract academic prose

result.description: Fires on function words and connectives (the, standard, comma, often, typically) in statistics and math explanations, just before a technical term such as deviation, test or measure. The same word elsewhere stays quiet, so topic matters.
result.label: Function words in statistics/math text

result.description: Fires on wh-words (' what', ' where', ' who') that open an embedded clause right after verbs like know, determine, understand, identify. Silent on 'what' in comparisons ("from what") or sentence-initial questions.
result.label: Embedded wh-word after know/determine

result.description: Fires on 'reflect' and its continuations (reflect, reflecting, reflects, depict) in text about culture or art reflecting values or beliefs. Silent on 'ing' in other verbs like drawing or challenging.

result.description: Fires on the verb ' goes' after a singular subject (It, a process, a sequence), mostly in the "X goes beyond ..." construction. Members detect go/goes/extends forms and "beyond" continuations.

result.description: Fires on mixed function words and punctuation (commas, 'the', 'to', 'and', word endings) inside abstract academic or scientific explanatory prose. The peaks are scattered, and the contrast also contains commas, so the condition is unclear.

result.description: Fires on the object of "take/takes" that expresses a duration, mainly " time" and also " hours" or " months" (e.g. "take some time", "may take hours"). It stays quiet on "time" in other constructions like "it's time to", "next time", "over time".

result.description: Fires on varied function words (to, by, of, do, in) following an abstract noun or participle in expository history/ideas text, e.g. "adherence to", "arrival of", "convinced by". Silent on many identical ' to' tokens; the pattern is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the token " press" (as in selection pressures, printing press, press freedom), where the word is a stem that could continue into "ures". Logits favor "ur"/"ures"-like continuations. Weaker on other word stems.

result.description: Fires on a comma that ends a clause about a turning point or major shift in a field, especially engineering or technology history (e.g. "a turning point in naval engineering,"). It is quiet on commas after other kinds of clauses.

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in abstract economics/systems prose, most strongly on 'term'/'run' in "long-term"/"short-run" and some verb or function-word slots. Silent on one "long-term success" case. Evidence is mixed and diffuse.

result.description: Fires on word pieces in thermodynamics terms: 'py' in "enthalpy" and ' Gib' in "Gibbs" free energy. It needs thermodynamics/chemistry context; members detect Gib, entropy, and chemistry terms.

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', 'ity', ' began', ' forms') in essays about ancient history, early art and symbols and cultural origins. It is silent on ' and' in other art or culture passages, so the pattern is diffuse.

result.description: Fires mostly on 'ent' inside "unrelenting" (after "unrel"), plus scattered other tokens such as commas and "other"/"goods". It stays silent on 'ent' in "prevalent", "relentless" and "sequent". Weak, mixed circuit.

result.description: Fires on verbs or function words right after a subject noun phrase describing a property or quantity (e.g. "weaker currency can", "longer bonds tend", "indicates"), in science and economics text. It sets up a comparative or causal relation (higher/stronger/than).
result.label: Verb after property-subject, comparative relation

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, and, or, to, involves) in abstract expository text about processes, skills, management or technical work, where a noun phrase is expected next. Peaks are mixed and contrast shows it silent on many 'the' tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in expository process text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'etic', mostly in "kinetic" (kinetic energy), also weakly in other -etic words. Members detect 'etic' and energy-physics context. Silent on thermal/heat text without the piece.

result.description: Fires on 'ged' in "emerged" (also "arose", "originated") when a movement, idea or school of thought is said to have appeared in a period. It stays silent on 'ged' in other words like "underprivileged".

result.description: Fires on the piece "per" inside botanical terms like "angiosperms" and "gymnosperms" (also "anippos-per-matos"). It stays quiet when the whole word "angiosperm" appears without a split "per" token.

result.description: Fires on function words and connectives (' by', ',', ' and', ' the', verb endings) in essay-style text about globalization and economic integration. Contrast shows it silent on ' by' in other topics, so it seems topic-dependent; the evidence is mixed.

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' Comput' (as in Cloud Computing, Affective Computing) in title or heading-like text, where the next piece is probably '-ing' or '-er'. Also weakly fires on ' Tre' and some heading tokens.

result.description: Fires on word-fragment tokens in the middle of a longer word, mainly ' mil' (before "estone"), also 'down' in "breakdown", 'eral', 'ys'. It seems to expect a suffix completing the word.

result.description: Fires on 'and' (or comma) before the last item in a list of colors, especially "red, yellow, and blue". Silent on 'and' in lists of non-color things like factors or names.
result.label: 'and' in color lists

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'w' piece inside split words like "fire|w|alls" and Kwak|w|aka, plus a few other word-internal pieces (' sp', 'el'). Members are detectors of 'w' mid-word. Predicts word continuations such as 'alls', 'oven'.

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ands" completing "demands" (dem|ands), especially in "demands on/placed on/of" in the sense of requirements or market pressures. Predicts "on", "placed", "for" next.
result.label: "ands" in "demands"

result.description: Fires on a noun right after an adjective or modifier in a descriptive phrase (hardened ends, intuitive control, piano keys, performance-critical applications). Peaks are mixed, with no single dominant token. Circuit is weak and diffuse.

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'itional' in "prepositional" (occasionally 'ial' in adverbial, 'inal' in nominal), in grammar-terminology text. Members detect prepos- word pieces and grammar terms like noun, conjunction.
result.label: 'itional' in prepositional

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' ev' when it begins a longer word, most often "as ev|idenced by", also "ev|aporation". Members detect other word-start fragments (em, aller, saf, cons) that need a continuation.
result.label: ' ev' word-start fragment (evidenced)

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words (within, in, each, they, other, plural -ers/-mers) in expository text about groups of actors (companies, composers, farmers) acting on or among each other. Peaks are inconsistent; it stays silent on some "within" tokens.
result.label: Group-actors function words, mixed

result.description: Fires on "improved" and "enhanced" (en|hanced) used as modifiers in lists of benefits or outcomes, e.g. "improved production efficiency, enhanced security". Members detect related comparatives like better, increased, improve.
result.label: improved/enhanced in benefit lists

result.description: Fires on varied word-start or abbreviation pieces, mostly ' Electron' in headings (e.g. "Role of Electron-"), 'GB' in "UGB", and some commas. Looks like a mixed, polysemantic latent. Members are mostly generic context.
result.label: Electron / GB mixed pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (commas, " of", " and", "including", partial word pieces) in abstract expository prose about regulation, economics or technique. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is diffuse, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered connectives in expository prose

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments such as ' Hard' (Hardware), ' Har' (Harbor, Harland) and ' tren' (trench), where the word is still incomplete. Members mostly detect ' hard' and similar word-start pieces.
result.label: Hard-/Har-/tren- word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on ' that' (also 'asserts', 'for') right after a verb or noun of claiming, such as emphasizes, posits, proposes, or the belief, in philosophy or theory text. It introduces a clause stating a doctrine's thesis. It stays silent on relative-clause 'that'.
result.label: Complement 'that' after doctrine-claiming verbs

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' political', ' communication', ' and', ' of', ' language') in academic text on geography, language and communication, mid-phrase after a noun like "aspects of" or "impact of". Silent on some ' political' contexts; the condition is unclear.
result.label: Academic geography/communication mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on function words (' a', ' the', ' in', ' to') right after "results in / formation of / leads to" in chemistry text, where a noun for a reaction outcome is expected. Silent on 'of a' describing properties or definitions.
result.label: Chemistry result-phrase function words

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' dup' (and occasionally ' decl') when it begins a longer word like "duplication"/"duplicated", mostly in biology/genetics text. Members are detectors of other incomplete word-start fragments (rep, comp, frag, susp).
result.label: ' dup' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on the piece 'al' completing "focal" (as in focal point/length), and weakly on ' quad' in quadrilaterals. It stays silent on 'al' in other words such as ideal, bilateral, ophthalmic.
result.label: 'al' in "focal"

result.description: Fires on function words or list items (" the", " and", commas, "other", "those") inside lists of issues or categories after "such as" or "like", in business or technical expository text. Peaks are scattered and silent on many " the" tokens, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Issue-list connectors in expository text

result.description: Fires mostly on ' ATP' in biochemistry text (ATP synthase, production, generation of ATP), and less often on ' Data' and list-item tokens. The peak token is mainly ' ATP', with a weaker secondary set of tokens.
result.label: ATP in biochemistry text

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'log' in crystallography, phylogenetic, syllogism, and on ' orth' / ' trig' in technical science words. It fires within scientific words being spelled out, with weaker hits on 'and' in lists of crystal systems.
result.label: Technical word fragment 'log' (crystallography)

result.description: Fires on mixed function words (' and', ' that', ' a', ' an') in abstract expository prose, mid-phrase where a noun phrase continues. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the exact condition is unclear. It is silent on some ' and' tokens in philosophy/math text.
result.label: Function words in abstract expository prose

result.description: Fires on varied verb-like or function tokens (making, improve, -ine in undermine, than, and, to) in essay-style text about communication and feedback, where a verb or object is expected next. Silent on 'ance' in 'enhance'. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Verb slots in communication essays

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (word pieces like 'ol', 'the', 'of', 'an') in abstract, expository text about engineering, technology and science, where a noun or verb is expected next. Evidence is mixed and the token pattern is weak.
result.label: Expository engineering text mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on varied connecting tokens ('-', ' where', ' without', ' from', ' to') in text about online or digital communication contrasted with traditional face-to-face interaction. It anticipates a next word like 'physical' or 'previous'. Silent on other hyphens.
result.label: Connectives in digital-vs-traditional communication

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (the, or, to, intent, how, use) in abstract explanatory prose about linguistics or concepts. Peaks are inconsistent, and the same ' the' is often silent, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in abstract expository prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'chan' in "mechan-" words, mainly biomechanics/mechanics (biomechanical, mechanics, mechanisms), and on capitalized ' Mechan' pieces. Members are detectors of chan/Mechan pieces that predict suffixes like -ical/-ics.
result.label: 'chan' piece in mechanics words

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' settled', ' in', ' on', ' of', ' through') in passages about the origins and early history of a field or civilization (agriculture, early computing, machine learning). Mixed peaks, low consistency; predicts nothing clearly.
result.label: Origins/early-history narrative tokens

result.description: Fires on the word "Theory"/"theory" (and weakly "theories") ending a named theory, such as "Uncertainty Reduction Theory" or "Arrhenius theory". Weaker on "this theory"/"this idea". Silent on unrelated statistics text.
result.label: Named "Theory" word

result.description: Fires on scattered word pieces in academic or science text (Dal- of Dalton, sci-fi, carbohydrate, social contract), often a first piece of a longer term. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the evidence is unclear.
result.label: Scattered word-start pieces in academic text

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (intricate, complex, mastery, a, s) in descriptions of a composer's or artist's style, such as Bach's intricate polyphony. Members are mostly music and art topic detectors. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Praise of composer's intricate style

result.description: Fires on function words (by, the, of, with) mid-sentence in abstract essay-style prose about writing, communication and storytelling. Peaks are scattered and the logits are not clear. The contrast shows no clear rule for when it stays silent.
result.label: Function words in writing-advice prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' pod' when it begins 'podcast', 'podcasting' or 'podcasters', and predicts 'cast' next. Members detect ' pod' and 'cast' pieces plus other word-initial fragments that need a continuation.
result.label: ' pod' before 'cast'

result.description: Fires on mixed function tokens, mostly ' (' after a temperature or numeric value (e.g. "375°C (175"), also ' and', ' capac' and a few word pieces. Silent on ' (' introducing prose asides. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Parenthesis after numeric units

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (digits, word fragments, ' or', ' for', ' medical') in explanatory, encyclopedic-style text. No consistent trigger or condition is visible; the circuit failed and members are generic.
result.label: Scattered tokens in explanatory text

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, to) and some nouns like 'hydro' in technical/scientific expository text, often after nouns like "flow characteristics of" or "into". Stays silent on 'the' in "one of the" or "nature of the". Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in technical prose
'od' in Thermodynamics
result.description: Fires on the token 'od' as the middle piece of "Thermodynamics" (e.g. "Law of Therm|od|ynamics"), predicting "ynamic" continuations. It is silent on 'od' in "thermodynamic quantities", and weakly active on similar pieces like 'ad' in "Faraday".

Fires on ' is' (sometimes ' are') right after an abstract noun subject such as "journey", "experience" or "road", before a predicate. It stays quiet after pronouns like "it" and in some other subjects.
result.label: ' is' after abstract noun subject

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, most often ' MongoDB' after "such as/like" in database text, plus function words (' a', ' offer', ' for') in technical software/database passages. Members are mostly generic technical-context attention heads. Peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: MongoDB and tech-text function words

result.description: Fires on pieces of the word "electro..." (' electro', 'imet' in electrogravimetry, 'ro' in Electrode) in electrochemistry text, especially when electrogravimetry/electroplating are listed. Silent on ' electro' before electrode/static in other contexts. Weak and mixed evidence.
result.label: electro- word pieces in electrochemistry

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' re' mid-word, mostly after nuclear, chemical or redox words, where it starts "reactions" or "reactor". Silent on some ' re' tokens in other contexts, such as at document start or after "spontaneous".
result.label: ' re' in nuclear/chemical reactions

result.description: Fires on the punctuation of "e.g.," / "i.e.," (the period or comma after "e.g") and sometimes a colon, when introducing a list of examples in linguistic or technical explanatory text. Silent on plain prose without such example markers.
result.label: e.g., example-introducing punctuation

result.description: Fires weakly on varied connective and list-position tokens (' and', ',', ' their', ' mixture', ' or') in academic, list-like text, but stays silent on many ' and' tokens in similar lists. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse list connectives in academic text

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly relative-clause ' which' and ' was' after it, plus ')', word pieces like 'ial', and hyphens. Silent on some ' which' after a comma in technical text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered ' which' and function tokens

result.description: Fires on prepositions (' in', ' for', ' to') right after an adjective of importance such as essential, crucial, fundamental or critical. It stays silent on 'in' in other slots, such as after nouns or verbs like 'proficiency in'.
result.label: Preposition after 'essential/crucial'

result.description: Fires mostly on the suffix 'ic' in words like Germanic or Strategic, with scattered peaks on ' to', 'l' and other tokens. It stays silent on 'ic' in acid-related words (acidic, phosphoric, electromagnetic). Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Suffix 'ic' (Germanic-type), mixed

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'acy' completing "privacy" (priv|acy), in text about data protection and consent. It stays silent when 'acy' starts a document with no preceding 'priv'.
result.label: 'acy' in "privacy"

result.description: Fires on ' perspective' (also 'point' in viewpoint) when it is a noun for a viewpoint, typically after adjectives like "unique" or "crucial" and before "on". Silent on technical "linear perspective" and sentence-initial use.
result.label: ' perspective' as viewpoint noun

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' leadership', 'ment', ' style', 'ation', ' which') in abstract academic/social-science prose about collaboration, empowerment and leadership. Mixed evidence; silent on some ' leadership' tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Abstract leadership/collaboration prose tokens
Word-initial fragments before continuation (py-)
result.description: Fires mostly on the word-start piece ' py' (as in pyruvate, pyramids) after glycolysis-type text. It also fires on a few other word-start fragments like 'cir', ' D' and a year's '1'. Members detect other prefix pieces expecting a suffix.

Fires on scattered function words (" the", " of", ",", " unique", " several") and the piece " G", mid-sentence in expository prose. Members are generic token detectors from list-like text; no clear shared trigger or condition.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires on the "ance" piece of the verb "enhance" (also "enhances", "improve"), mainly in food and flavor text, predicting an object like taste or flavor. Silent on "ance" in nouns like "fragrance".
result.label: enhance verb, "-ance" piece

result.description: Fires on the word " number" (also "Number"), mostly as a head noun in "the number of…" or "a number of", and in math contexts like "natural number" or "quantum number". Members are mostly " number" detectors.
result.label: the word "number"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' las' / ' Las' (before 'er') and on 'polym'/'ym' in 'polymer', i.e. word fragments that need a suffix like '-er' to complete. Mostly in technical science text; predicts the completing suffix.
result.label: las- / polym- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the word " bare" (as in "bare bones", "bare minimum", "bare ground"), often in metaphorical or analogy phrasing. Members detect bare and similar adjectives like plain, raw, empty, open. Next-token logits are mixed.
result.label: ' bare' adjective token

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' By' when it begins "Byzantine" after "the" (mid-sentence), predicting a continuation like 'zan'. Silent when Byzantine is the first token of the document. Weak activity on other word-start fragments.
result.label: By- start of Byzantine

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens in physics-flavored text, mostly 'ons' (phonons), ' force', and 'ification'. The logits favor motion verbs like pushing, moving and driving. The 'ons' peak is silent in 'silencerons', so it needs a physics context.
result.label: Physics force/phonon terms

result.description: Fires on words meaning subtle or slight, mostly the 'le' in "subtle", also " slight", "slightest" and "quiet", in descriptions of small, understated gestures or changes. Predicts "ty" or "yet" continuations weakly.
result.label: subtle / slight understatement words

result.description: Fires on the 'ist' piece of 'twist' (also twists, twisty) in writing-advice text about plot twists. It stays silent on 'ist' in 'protagonist', so it needs the word-piece after 'tw'.
result.label: 'ist' in 'twist'

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (' mark', apostrophe, digits, 'ations', mid-word pieces) with low consistency. No clear shared trigger or condition. It appears to fire mid-word or mid-phrase in expository text, where a continuation is expected.
result.label: Scattered mid-word pieces, unclear

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments and some function words (im, ason, bol, ' in', 'ever') where a word is incomplete or being continued; peaks are scattered with no single token. Contrast shows silence on 'im' inside other words like polymers.
result.label: Scattered word-piece fragments, low consistency
Digits inside long decimal numbers
result.description: Fires on mid-number digit tokens, especially '0' and '1' in long decimals or figures like 1.6180339 or 6,000, plus occasional 've' word pieces. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak and mixed.

Fires on varied tokens (weather, visual, ver-, statistical, 2, and) that start a modifier or noun in the middle of an abstract academic phrase; peaks are scattered and low-consistency. The evidence does not show a clear shared trigger.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase academic modifiers

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ym' piece in "Polymer" in a list of academic field or journal titles (Polymer Science/Engineering), with weaker hits on ' loss', ' data', ' step'. Members are diffuse and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: 'ym' in Polymer titles

result.description: Fires mostly on ' Festival' (especially in "Music Festival" headings), plus scattered nouns like ' evolution', ' valley', ' arc'. Festival-detecting members are discriminative; the rest is mixed, so the target looks polysemantic.
result.label: Festival plus scattered nouns

result.description: Fires on ' used' (also employed/applied) as a reduced relative participle right after a plural noun like "methodologies used" or "techniques used", in expository text. It is silent on ' used' in passive or active verb uses.
result.label: Post-noun participle 'used' (techniques used)

result.description: Fires on a standalone 'v' token (or ' V'/' v') that begins a word split into pieces, e.g. 'v' in sous-vide, vague, curviness, v4. Also fires on ' Rob' in 'in Robotics'. Predicts continuations like 'ague', 'antage', 'ular'.
result.label: Word-initial 'v' fragment

result.description: Fires on function words (' to', ',', ' the') in explanations of experimental design and statistics, especially "assigning sample units/participants to ... groups". Silent on ' to' in other topics. Logits are unclear; the circuit fails.
result.label: Function words in randomization/experiment text

result.description: Fires mostly on ' L' in "L1, L2" style lists and on adjectives before technical nouns (raw, executable, finished, machine) in compiler/computing text. Mixed peaks; the circuit is diffuse and its members are mostly generic attention latents.
result.label: ' L' and modifiers in compiler text

result.description: Fires on the piece "o" in "stereo" (Stere|o) when the word is split into tokens, e.g. "stereo vision" or "stereo image". It stays quiet on a standalone "o". Predicts word-continuation pieces such as "ots", "ters", "estig".
result.label: "o" inside split word "stereo"

result.description: Fires on the subword piece 'ios' inside scientific words, mainly 'meiosis' and 'bio-' compounds (biosensors, biosemiotics). Members detect 'ios', 'mos', 'otos' and 'os' pieces in technical biology terms. Weaker on 'osa' and 'orm'.
result.label: 'ios' piece in biology terms

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens: word fragments, gibberish Cyrillic pieces, " brand", " former", "as", mostly in linguistics/grammar text. No dominant token or clear condition; the peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered word-piece fragments, grammar text

result.description: Fires on the plural noun ' factors' (also areas, concepts, considerations) right after adjectives like "key", "primary", "crucial" in a "X and Y are the key factors" predicate. Silent on "combination of factors" or "environmental factors".
result.label: Key/important 'factors' predicate noun
Sentence-ending period in philosophy text
result.description: Fires on the period ending a sentence in abstract philosophy passages (idealism, realism, mathematical truth), occasionally on ' and'. It stays silent on periods in other contexts, such as logic or narrative text and abbreviations like "i.e.".

Fires on causal verbs like "brought" (about) and "usher-ed" (in) after a historical or technological change as subject (Industrial Revolution, internet), predicting "about/in" and a result such as a new era or changes.
result.label: Change-bringing verbs: brought about, ushered in

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' batt' (also ' brut') when it begins a longer word like battles, battled or battlements. It expects a continuation such as '-les'. Weakly fires on similar word-start pieces like 'un-orth'.
result.label: ' batt' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on ' which' (sometimes ' that') introducing a relative clause after a comma or noun, mostly in technical or process descriptions (techniques, methods). Contrast shows it is silent on some ' which' after scientific nouns like colloids, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Relative 'which' after technique nouns

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (Victorian's 'ian', year digits, 'of', 'and') in essay-like text about literary or historical periods and story structure. It predicts academic field words such as 'sciences' and 'fields'. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Literary and historical period essays

result.description: Fires on the word "conversation" and its pieces ("convers" + "ations", also "dialogue"), mostly as an object of verbs like engage in or facilitate. Members are mostly conversation/discussion detectors. Predicts little clearly.
result.label: conversation word

result.description: Fires on incomplete word pieces in the middle of a longer word, mainly 'RI' in MRI, ' indust' (industries) and 'opol' (geopolitics, monopolistic). Members are word-start fragment detectors that expect a suffix continuation.
result.label: Mid-word fragments: RI, indust, opol

result.description: Fires on varied words in science text about pairing, bonding, or working together (pairs, together, bond, between, complementary, atom). It stays silent on the "-ate" verb ending in words like "resonate" or "curate", so it tracks the interaction sense, not the token.
result.label: Pairing/bonding and cooperation words

result.description: Fires on the ' B' in immunology text about B cells (B cell, BCR, B lymphocyte), in adaptive-immune-response contexts. Silent on at least one 'B cell' example, so the condition is not fully clear.
result.label: B in B-cell immunology

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in academic or explanatory text (word endings like "comes", "al", " them", " A", " where"), with no dominant token. It is silent on "comes" in one similar context. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in academic text

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'eg' inside longer words (vinegar, electronegativity, Hegel, Kierkegaard), and sometimes the hyphen in "Agenda-Setting". It needs the piece to sit within a word that is still being completed.
result.label: 'eg' word-piece inside words

result.description: Fires on ' in' right after an abstract academic noun or adjective, such as "a concept in" or "prevalent in", where "the field of" or an area of study comes next. Silent on ' in' after "occurred" or "strides".
result.label: ' in' before "the field of"

result.description: Fires on varied adjective-like or modifier tokens (conceptual's "ual", abstract, physical, hypothetical) in an explanatory passage about abstract models. Silent on "conceptualizing". Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weakly faithful.
result.label: Abstract/conceptual modifier tokens in explanations

result.description: Fires on problem-type nouns (issues, challenges, difficulties, problems) that are the object of "address/addressing/facing" verbs. Silent on "scalability issues" in a plain list, so it seems to need the addressing/handling construction.
result.label: Challenges/issues as object of addressing

result.description: Fires on the end of a role or agent noun (leader, baker, dabbler, teacher, designer) in "transform/turn from an ordinary X into a skilled Y" framing. Silent on 'ist' in non-agent words like twist or protagonist.
result.label: Agent noun in transformation phrase
PI in PPI acronym
result.description: Fires on the 'PI' token completing the acronym PPI (protein-protein interactions), and sometimes on '0' in long runs of zeros. Members detect final pieces of capitalized acronyms and biology terms.

Fires on the word-piece ' curr' when it starts a longer word such as currents or curriculum, after a preceding word. It is silent when ' curr' begins the text. Weak activation on a few other word pieces.
result.label: ' curr' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on "complexity" and the "-ities" of "complexities", especially in "capture the complexities of human thought/nature" phrasing. It is silent on other text. It predicts verbs and abstract continuations only weakly.
result.label: complexity / complexities noun

result.description: Fires mostly on the ' fa' piece of "fauna" (e.g. "Biogeographic fauna") in biogeography/ecology text, with weaker firing on assorted list items and function words. Peaks are mixed, so the pattern is partial.
result.label: ' fa' in fauna (biogeography)

result.description: Fires on prepositions or verbs (to, in, for, fosters) right after "understanding is essential/crucial/aids", where the next word is likely a comprehension verb like grasp or appreciate. Silent on "in" after other adjectives or nouns.
result.label: Preposition after 'understanding is essential'

result.description: Fires mostly on the token " For" (also "for", "To", " that"), especially "For" at sentence start or as the piece in "Random Forests" before "instance/example". Members detect "for" variants and "for example" continuations.
result.label: "For" token, "for instance" style

result.description: Fires on ' thousands' in "hundreds to thousands of" quantity phrases and on the 'struct' piece of "unstructured/structured". The two peaks are different tokens, and the weaker contexts are scattered.
result.label: ' thousands' and 'struct' (unstructured)

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and connectors (' and', ',', 'gradually', 'with', 'within', '+') mid-phrase in abstract expository prose. No single token dominates; ' and' is often silent in lists, so the evidence is mixed and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered connectors in expository prose

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments (' mon', ' unf', ' im', ' pro', 'lig') in legal and economic text, where the next piece completes a word like monetary, unfair, imbalance, prosecution or negligence. Members are mostly legal and regulatory topic detectors.
result.label: Legal word-start fragments (mon-, unf-, im-)

result.description: Fires on noun stems like institution, instrument, exception, monument, element when they are likely to be followed by an '-al' or '-ation' suffix (institutional, instrumental, exceptional). Predicts 'al', 'ality', 'ally'.
result.label: Stem before -al suffix

result.description: Fires on words meaning "foundation" in the metaphorical sense (foundation, basis, bedrock, cornerstone) after "forms/is the", where something is described as the underpinning of other concepts. Predicts "for" or "of".
result.label: Foundation/basis metaphor nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment ' ob' (mostly in "objection(s)"), plus a few other word-initial pieces like ' meta', ' dest', ' TH'. Contrast shows it is silent when the whole word is used instead of the split piece.
result.label: ' ob' fragment in 'objection'

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' of', ' in', ' for', 'ernel', 'term', 'CM') in technical or expository text, often mid-term or in a noun phrase. Peaks are inconsistent and ' of' is often silent. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical text

result.description: Fires mainly on 'light' inside "Enlightenment" (and 'en' pieces), plus slashes within numeric or fraction-like strings such as "2/3/4" or "15/18". Silent on slashes between words or in "9/11". Mixed, with two distinct triggers.
result.label: Enlightenment 'light' and numeric slashes

result.description: Fires on the word stems " induct" and " predict" (also "predict" in "unpredictable") when they are unfinished word pieces, just before a suffix like -ive, -able or -or. It predicts these suffixes next.
result.label: induct/predict stem before -ive

result.description: Fires on the ending of a culture/people/civilization adjective or demonym (Islamic, Arab, Mesopotamian, Ottoman, Armenian) in historical-cultural text, predicting nouns like Empire, region or period. Silent on 'ic' in prehistoric or monolithic.
result.label: Ethnic/cultural adjective endings in history

result.description: Fires on plural endings ('s', 'ors', 'es') attached to a noun stem, mostly in 'strengths' (strengths/weaknesses) and 'flavors'. It stays silent on apostrophe-'s' and on other plurals like 'resolutions'.
result.label: Plural suffix after noun stem

result.description: Fires on the closing piece 'sky' of a surname, mainly Chomsky, also other word-final pieces (het, op, edia). Members detect surname endings (Kahneman, Thaler, Einstein, Tversky) in academic text.
result.label: Surname ending 'sky' (Chomsky)

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yl', mostly the end of "vinyl" (records, streaming, CDs), and also in words like syllogisms and acetylation. Silent when 'yl' starts a text with no preceding piece.
result.label: 'yl' piece, esp. vinyl

result.description: Fires on ' syntax' as a noun (language syntax) and on the 'D' ending the acronym QKD. Silent on related words like 'syntactic constituents'. Members include syntax detectors and capital-letter fragments; the circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: ' syntax' and acronym 'D' (QKD)

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' cl' (clay, clues, clutter, cloning) and ' hum' (humidity), where a word is split into pieces and the next piece continues it. Predicts continuations like 'ues', 'aturing', 'otted'.
result.label: Split-word ' cl' / ' hum' fragments

result.description: Fires on the first word or piece of a noun phrase right after "the rise/advent/emergence/proliferation of" (e.g. digital, nation, professional, civil-). It likely predicts modern-era innovations like "Online" or "mod". Silent on "digital" elsewhere.
result.label: Modifier after "the rise of"

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' empir' (before -ical/-icism), occasionally ' aggregate'. Members are detectors of ' empir' and similar incomplete stems (induct-, inqu-, Class-, graph-) that precede an -ical/-ive suffix.
result.label: ' empir' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on ' moral' and on 'etic' in 'Aesthetic' (also weakly ' economic', 'aesthetic'), in philosophy/ethics-style text where a value-type adjective precedes a noun like judgment, values, or obligation. Members are mostly ' moral' detectors.
result.label: moral / aesthetic value adjective

result.description: Fires on past participles like "improved", "refined", "enhanced" used predicatively after "is/were/are" (passive verb slot), often before a "by/through/thanks" phrase. Silent when "improved" is an attributive adjective before a noun ("and improved productivity").
result.label: Passive improved/enhanced participle
