result.description: Fires on the word " dynamic" (also " Dynamic") when used as a modifier before a noun, as in "dynamic systems", "dynamic programming", "dynamic range". It is silent when the word starts a text with no preceding context.
result.label: " dynamic" as adjective modifier

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces like "ance", "ence" or "ray" in names of spectroscopy and resonance techniques (nuclear magnetic resonance, X-ray fluorescence). It stays silent on "ance" in unrelated words such as "abundance". Predicts "Spect" continuations.
result.label: Resonance/spectroscopy technique name endings

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "ations" when it completes "expectations" (expect|ations). It stays silent on "ations" in other words such as foundations, collaborations and negotiations. Output pushes towards "expect", "expectation", "about", "regarding".
result.label: "ations" ending "expectations"

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments inside longer words, mainly 'ific' (Sign-ific-ance, Art-ific-ial) and 'mean' (mean-ings), plus similar pieces like 'vere', 'est', 'ask'. Predicts suffix continuations such as 'ant', 'ance', 'ings'.
result.label: Mid-word fragments ific/mean

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ber' in "reverberation" (rever|ber|ation), in acoustics text. Members mostly detect 'ber' after 'rever' or similar word-internal pieces.
result.label: 'ber' inside reverberation

result.description: Fires on the piece 'geon' in "burgeoning" (bur|geon), right after 'bur', and predicts a suffix like 'ing' or 'ed'. Appears in growth-of-an-era text. Silent in contrast text without this word.
result.label: 'geon' in burgeoning

result.description: Fires on the verb " allows" (also " allow") after a subject noun such as a technique or abstraction, predicting " for" or a beneficiary next. It is silent when " allows" starts the text with no subject before it.
result.label: ' allows' after a subject

result.description: Fires on the final token of workplace-outcome nouns in lists of organizational results (morale, productivity, turnover rates, customer satisfaction), usually after "lower/higher/improved". The contrast shows silence outside such outcome lists.
result.label: Workplace outcome metric nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece " multip" at the start of "multiplicity", mostly in linear algebra text about algebraic and geometric multiplicity. It predicts the continuation "licity". Members detect " multip" and similar word-start fragments.
result.label: " multip" before "licity"

result.description: Fires on mixed positions in generic expository prose, mostly sentence-end periods, " reson" (before ate/ance), "also" and "establish". Silent on many periods in similar text. Predicts verb-like continuations such as "themselves", "support", "unfold". Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Mixed periods and 'reson' in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the '0' token right after a leading '2' in year-like numbers (2008, 2013, 20th century, 2020). It stays silent on '0' in other positions such as 2004, 1970, or 210.
result.label: Second digit '0' in 20xx years

result.description: Fires on ' just' right after "beyond" or "more than", in the "not limited to just X" sense. It stays silent on ' just' after "not" or "are" (e.g. "are just like"). Members detect just/mere/simply/only plus "beyond".
result.label: 'just' after 'beyond'/'more than'

result.description: Fires on the 'ent' piece completing "underwent" (also 'un-pre' of "unprecedented"), typically in "X underwent a significant transformation". Silent on 'ent' in other words like "prevalent".
result.label: 'ent' in "underwent"

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces or word continuations (emble, fect, factor, iving, ged, um) inside multi-token words or names, often in lists of short headings. Peaks are scattered and the logits are mixed, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Mid-word piece continuation, scattered

result.description: Fires on separators (comma, "and", "or", slash) after a named item in an example list of proper names (methods, tools, auction houses, artists), as in "such as Otsu and ...". Predicts another name next. Silent on commas after common phrases.
result.label: Separator after listed example names

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ical' in "Biomedical" at the start of a document or title (also 'ot' in "Robotics"). It stays silent on 'ical' in Mechanical, Spherical, Lexical and Statistical, so it seems tied to this particular word.
result.label: Biomedical 'ical' / Robotics 'ot' pieces

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'id' inside longer words, mainly 'mer-id-ian' (prime meridian), also Dravidian, Procyonidae, subsidies. Mostly a mid-word 'id' piece; a few weak hits on other word fragments.
result.label: 'id' piece in meridian-type words

result.description: Fires on ' Great' as part of a proper name or historical term, such as "the Great Depression", "the Great War", "Great Lakes" or "Sejong the Great". Predicts continuations like War, Britain or Fire. Members mostly detect ' Great' and similar name-leading words.
result.label: ' Great' in proper names

result.description: Fires on the 'est' piece in "celestial" (also weakly on ' plan'/' planet' in astronomy text), predicting the continuation 'ial'. Silent on 'est' in "aesthetic", so it needs the cel- prefix context.
result.label: 'est' in "celestial"

result.description: Fires on word pieces in physics text that precede Einstein-related or relativity/kinetic terms, such as ' Albert' before Einstein, ' kin' in kinetic, ' relativ', and ' Lor' in Lorentz. It predicts ' Ein' next.
result.label: Albert/kin- in relativity physics

result.description: Fires mostly on fragments of multi-byte or corrupted characters (replacement-character tokens in CJK or Arabic text) and on scattered tokens like ' solutions' and 'ives'. The peaks are mixed and the circuit's own evidence is weak.
result.label: Broken multibyte character fragments

result.description: Fires on the token ' distribution' as a noun for how things are spread (species, electrons, products), mostly after "the". It is silent when the word starts a text with no preceding context. It pushes toward ' pattern(s)'.
result.label: ' distribution' noun after determiner

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied noun-ending word pieces and nouns in expository or academic text (e.g. 'ulation', 'recovery', 'environmental', 'ures'). The peaks share no single token or construction, and the circuit looks diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse academic noun-ending pieces

result.description: Fires on ' in' (sometimes ' on') right after a verb and its object in cooking or process instructions, introducing the medium or container, such as cooking food in boiling water or cooling in ice water. It stays silent on 'in' after nouns or inside words.
result.label: 'in' after verb+object, cooking medium

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'avel' in 'wavelength(s)', after the 'w' start of the word. It predicts 'ength' next. It stays silent when 'avel' begins the text with no preceding 'w'.
result.label: 'avel' in wavelength

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ings'/'ation' completing error words like misunderstandings or misinterpretation, and occasionally 'and' after confusion, in text about cross-cultural communication problems. Silent on 'ings' in 'meanings'.
result.label: Misunderstand-ings suffix in communication errors

result.description: Fires in text about tree data structures (binary trees, BST) on words like "data", "efficient", "-based", "-like" that precede a structure noun. Predicts tree/node/leaf/indexing. Silent on "data" in generic data-quality contexts.
result.label: Tree data-structure modifier words

result.description: Fires on the word " original" used as an adjective after a determiner or possessive (the original language, your original content), meaning the first or source version. It predicts nouns like source, author, text.
result.label: " original" as adjective

result.description: Fires on the last token of a science or philosophy topic noun (atom, magnetism, gases, perception) inside a "X's Law/Model of [topic]" phrase naming a scientist's work. It predicts verbs like laid, established, introduced. Silent on the same suffixes in other contexts.
result.label: Topic noun ending a named-theory phrase

result.description: Fires on the word-final piece 'us' in 'Celsius' (also weakly on endings like -at, -as, -ds, -ation, -ium), in science/heat-and-temperature text. Upstream members include heat/cooking/temperature detectors and 'us' detectors.
result.label: Celsius word-ending 'us' piece

result.description: Fires on digit tokens (9, 8, 6, 7) in approximate numeric quantities such as "around 70%", "approximately 299,7…", "75°F", mostly in science text. Silent on a digit inside a year like 1905.
result.label: Digits in approximate measurements

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verb pieces (to, of, -ining, -ving, tips, guidance) in expository or technical text where a verb or noun is about to take an object or complement. Weak, mixed evidence; silent on purpose-clause "to".
result.label: Function words before objects, technical prose

result.description: Fires on quality adjectives or adjective pieces (proper, effective, -ive, -ful, efficient) that precede a noun in writing about communication, predicting nouns like use, usage, consideration. Silent when "proper" starts the document.
result.label: Quality adjectives before a noun

result.description: Fires on connectors (' and', ' to', ' or', ' through', '-') right after a decade expression like "the 1990s", where a range continues ("and into the early…", "to the early…"). Silent on 'and' joining ordinary nouns or clauses.
result.label: Connector after decade in time range

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ent' in the word "patent" (pat|ent), including "patentable", in intellectual property text. It stays silent on 'ent' in other words such as "intelligent". Weak activation on a few other word pieces.
result.label: 'ent' in pat-ent

result.description: Fires on word stems that are incomplete and need a suffix such as -y, -iness or -ing (' breath', 'itt', ' color', ' dress'), in essay-style prose. It predicts suffix pieces like 'y', 'iness' and 'ty'. The peaks are mixed and activation is weak.
result.label: Word stems awaiting suffix (breath, itt)

result.description: Fires on commas, slashes, or "or" after a demographic category like race, age or gender in a list of social categories. It predicts the next category, such as religion, race or sexual. Other lists of abstract nouns stay silent.
result.label: Demographic category list separators

result.description: Fires on plural place nouns like towns, cities, streets, homes, mostly in urbanization or industrialization text. It predicts words like "folk", "filled" or "built". The contrast is abstract digital/personal text, where it stays silent.
result.label: Plural settlement nouns in urban text

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments such as 'enc' in "stencil" and 'ir' in "aspirations", "chirp" and "Stirling", plus occasional divider dashes. The next token is a word continuation. Mostly word-piece detectors.
result.label: Mid-word pieces 'enc'/'ir' (stencil, aspirations)

result.description: Fires on ' more' used as a comparative determiner/modifier directly before a noun or adjective (after "for", "to", "of", "by", "in"), as in "need for more straightforward". It stays silent on ' more' after linking verbs like "became/be/are".
result.label: ' more' as noun-phrase comparative

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments like ' Me', 'mm', ' tre' that begin a word whose continuation is likely 'asures'/'asure' (Measures, treasures), also Meissner, dilemmas. Predicts 'as...' continuations.
result.label: Me- fragment predicting 'asures'

result.description: Fires on a comma right after a short name or list item, such as a surname in "Surname, Given name" catalog entries or an item in a list of nouns. It is silent on commas that follow a clause and introduce a participial phrase.
result.label: Comma after name or list item

result.description: Fires on the word " combined" used as a participle, usually after a noun phrase and a comma ("factors, combined with…"). It predicts "with" or "together" next. Members are mostly detectors of combine/combined/blended.
result.label: ' combined' participle before 'with'

result.description: Fires on the word " why" introducing a subordinate clause after verbs like understand, explain, explore, or "reasons"/"is why". It predicts the clause subject (certain, some, we, they).
result.label: " why" after explain/understand

result.description: Fires on word-initial or mid-word fragments that need a continuation, mostly ' prospect' (prospect theory, prospects), also 'uct' in infrastructure, ' divis', ' conject'. Predicts suffix pieces like 'inals' or 'ican'.
result.label: Incomplete word fragments, mainly 'prospect'

result.description: Fires on function words (" the", " from", " of", " occurred") in descriptions of geological eras and periods (Cenozoic, Paleogene, Eocene), especially before dates or the next era name. Silent on " the" in other historical or general contexts.
result.label: Function words in geological era text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' st' when it starts a split word, mostly the 'st' of "stakeholder" after "strategic" or "stake", and also in "Stellar" and "strive". It predicts continuations like 'ake', 'riv' and 'ems'.
result.label: ' st' word-start piece (stakeholder)

result.description: Fires on the demonstrative " these" as a determiner before a plural noun, mostly after a verb or preposition (monitor these, in light of these). Members are mostly detectors of "these" and "this". It predicts a following plural noun.
result.label: demonstrative " these" before plural noun

result.description: Fires on the token piece "oga" completing the word "Yoga" (Karma Yoga, Jnana Yoga, Purpose of Yoga), in text about Indian philosophy. Members are mostly "oga" detectors plus Buddhism/Hindu-term members.
result.label: "oga" in Yoga

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' r' when it begins a longer word, mostly "rhetoric/rhetorical", also "ratios" and "rasa". Predicts continuation pieces like 'het'. Silent when the word is not split after ' r'.
result.label: ' r' start of "rhetoric"

result.description: Fires on plural policy-type nouns (initiatives, strategies, measures, practices, policies) that end a noun phrase in sustainability or management text, often as a subject before a verb like "must" or "can". Silent on some "strategies" in other phrasing.
result.label: Plural strategy/measure nouns as subject

result.description: Fires on ' Otto' (Otto Cycle) and the 'antine' piece of 'Byzantine', plus occasional name fragments. Two specific word pieces, supported by members detecting 'antine' and medieval/historical context.
result.label: Otto and Byzantine word pieces

result.description: Fires on the token piece 'AP' inside capitalized acronyms such as CAPM, CAPT, SAP and APO, mostly in finance or business text. Upstream members are mainly 'AP' token detectors.
result.label: 'AP' in acronyms (CAPM, SAP)

result.description: Fires on determiners, possessives or modifier pieces right after "align(ed/ing) with" (e.g. "with the", "with their", "company's"), where the next word would be goals, objectives or interests. Silent on "the" elsewhere.
result.label: Object slot after "align with"

result.description: Fires on a comma that follows a completed sentence, right after a period, where a new clause starts in lowercase. Stays silent on ordinary mid-sentence commas after clauses or phrases.
result.label: Comma right after sentence-ending period

result.description: Fires on plural nouns for people or things (words, people, stories, individuals) right after "the" or "and the" in a coordinated noun phrase. Predicts "themselves/involved". Silent on "words" after adjectives or prepositions like "in other words".
result.label: Plural noun after "the" (people/things)

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", or "like" after a method or analysis type inside a list of research or analysis methods (e.g. "methods include qualitative content analysis, ..."). It predicts further method nouns such as analysis, reviews, regression. Silent on commas in general prose.
result.label: List separators in analysis-method lists

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' met' when it begins a longer word like metallic, metaphor, metabolic or metamorphosis. It predicts continuations such as 'aph', 'abol' and 'icul'.
result.label: ' met' as word-start piece

result.description: Fires on a domain noun ending a compound topic phrase (pottery-making, music production, naval architecture, industry) after "a turning point/breakthrough in the history of X", just before a verb like "occurred" or "marked". Silent in "smaller-scale production processes".
result.label: Field noun after "turning point in"

result.description: Fires on abstract nouns ending a noun phrase about availability or latitude (flexibility, support, freedom, resources, investment), often after "little", "more", or "lack of". Logits favor "than", "available", "due", "compared".
result.label: Abstract nouns of flexibility/support/resources

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments ' kn' (as in knot) and ' erg' (as in ergonomic), plus a few other word-starting pieces. Predicts continuations completing the word (e.g. 'ot', 'onomic'-like suffixes). Mostly seen in technical, abstract text.
result.label: kn- / erg- word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on word endings (-es, -ements, -acy, -ement) completing achievement/success nouns like "successes", "achievements", "supremacy". Silent on -es in unrelated words like "poses" or "businesses". Members detect success/achievement stems.
result.label: Suffix of success/achievement nouns

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (that, a, of, match, postulates, linking) that introduce a described relation or object in explanatory, technical prose. Peaks are scattered and the contrast is not clearly separable, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Function words in explanatory technical prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'aph' inside split words, mostly "met|aph|ors" and also "An|aph|ase" and "met|aph|ysics". Upstream members are mostly 'aph' detectors. Logits favor suffix pieces like 'ent' and 'rable'.
result.label: 'aph' piece in metaphor

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' w' (a space-prefixed 'w' that starts a split word), mostly in economics text before 'ages'/'age' (wage), and also before welfare, wavelength, wool. It pushes towards continuations like 'ages', 'elf', 'oven'.
result.label: word-initial ' w' fragment (wage)

result.description: Fires on the nouns " titles" and " status" (also " title", " value") in discussion of social rank, honorifics, capitalization of job titles, and prestige. Members include detectors of " titles" and " status" (as in "status quo") and prestige-related tokens.
result.label: titles / status nouns

result.description: Fires on the word piece "rom" inside "aromatic"/"aroma" (after "a"), also in "achromatic". Members mostly detect "rom" in these words. Weak activation on other mid-word pieces.
result.label: "rom" in aroma/aromatic

result.description: Fires on the opening parenthesis ' (' after a technical or scientific term (e.g. nitrogen, plant hormones, particulate matter), where an abbreviation, symbol or clarification follows. It stays silent when the term is in a plain list without a parenthesis.
result.label: Parenthesis after technical term

result.description: Fires on the final piece of abstract nouns, mostly plural or suffix endings (-ities, -ation, halls, periods, landscape, intervals) in academic prose. Silent on the contraction 's (it's, muse's). Peaks are mixed and weakly consistent.
result.label: Abstract noun endings in academic prose

result.description: Fires on the token " Berlin", mostly in Cold War history contexts (Berlin Wall, Berlin Blockade, holdings in Berlin). Many members detect Berlin itself. Weak activation on " air" and " Napoleon".
result.label: Berlin token (Cold War contexts)

result.description: Fires on the token ' do' (also ' did') when it is a word-start fragment of a longer word, such as 'dopamine', 'doping', 'dozens' or 'didactic', not the auxiliary verb. Predicts continuations like 'z', 'ctr', 'actic'.
result.label: ' do' as word-start fragment

result.description: Fires in lists or pairs of contrasting aspects (advantages and dis-, strengths and weak-, benefits and costs) at the point where a negative counterpart such as disadvantages, weaknesses, limitations or challenges is expected next.
result.label: Predicts disadvantages/weaknesses after positives

result.description: Fires on technical process nouns (reduction, identification, extraction, purification, conservation) ending a compound in technical/engineering text, where a noun like "strategies/techniques/methods" often follows. Silent on verb forms like "reduce/reducing".
result.label: Technical process nouns like reduction

result.description: Fires on the word " deep"/" Deep" (as in deep learning, deep connections, deepening), with weaker firing on "ep" in "steeped". Predicts continuations like -ening/-ened. Members are mostly earlier "deep" detectors.
result.label: deep token detector

result.description: Fires on a capital letter (mostly D, also B, N, MA) inside an uppercase acronym being spelled out, such as GDPR, DAC, MAC, SSD or R&D. It mostly predicts the acronym's next letters, such as 'PR'.
result.label: Acronym letters, especially D

result.description: Fires on varied tokens about origin or derivation (' derived', ' translated', 'etched', 'deriving', ' Mit' pieces) in historical or cultural prose. Logits favor ' as' and quote marks. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Derived/translated origin words, mixed

result.description: Fires on ' a' (occasionally ' an') right after a document-opening "In", as in "In a schoolyard setting…". Silent on ' a' elsewhere, such as after verbs or inside words like "akin".
result.label: "In a" at document start

result.description: Fires on ' drum' (and ' hip' in hip hop) in music text, often as a word-start before a suffix like -mer, -ming, -head. Silent on general music prose without these words. Members are music-genre and instrument detectors.
result.label: drum / hip in music contexts

result.description: Fires on the word " advanced" / " Advanced" used as an adjective before a noun (advanced level, advanced topics, advanced technology). Pushes towards nouns like topics, levels, versions, stages. Members are mostly "advanced" token detectors.
result.label: Adjective "advanced" before noun

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments inside particular words: 'id' in humidity, 'fert'/'il' in fertile/fertilizer/fertilization, weakly 'explos' in explosion. It predicts suffixes like -ification, -ity.
result.label: hum-id-ity / fert-ilizer word pieces

result.description: Fires on articles (' a', ' the', ' an') right after a verb like "provide", "forms", "embodying" in expository science or technical text, where an evaluative noun such as "cornerstone" or "fundamental" is expected. Silent on articles after prepositions or "but".
result.label: Article after descriptive verb, expository

result.description: Fires on word-ending suffix pieces like -ization, -ologies, -ies, -cies completing abstract plural or noun forms, mostly in energy/engineering text ("energy utilization strategies", "conversion technologies"). Silent on "ionization" in a chemistry-like context.
result.label: Abstract noun suffixes in energy text

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'est' when it sits inside a longer word, such as A-est-hetic, Under-est-imation, cel-est-ial or liv-est-ock. It is silent on ordinary text without that piece. It pushes toward continuations like 'het', 'imation' and 'ock'.
result.label: 'est' mid-word fragment

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ont" inside "sp-ont-aneous" (and "spontaneity"), predicting "aneous". It is silent when "ont" starts the text without the "sp" before it.
result.label: "ont" in "spontaneous"

result.description: Fires on the articles ' a' / ' an' right after "marked by", "characterized by", "galvanized by" or similar verbs, where an abstract noun like shift, growth or focus comes next. Silent on "as an" and "within an".
result.label: Article after "marked by" (abstract change)

result.description: Fires on ' arguments' / ' argument' as a noun in discussions of persuasion, logic and reasoning, after modifiers like compelling, persuasive or logical. Silent when the word starts the text with no preceding context.
result.label: argument(s) in reasoning text

result.description: Fires on the piece "al" completing the word "peripheral" (peripher|al), after the "peripher" fragment. It stays silent on "al" in other words such as instrumental, ribosomal or isochronal.
result.label: "al" in "peripheral"

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens (commas, 'ization', 'AD', 'ate', '(') in abstract academic or philosophical prose. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast also contains commas, so the evidence for a specific trigger is thin.
result.label: Scattered tokens in abstract academic prose

result.description: Fires on the first or middle piece of a rare proper name split into word pieces (Z, Zaris-ki, Rob-bins, Arc-angelo), mostly in lists of names. It pushes toward continuation pieces like 'O', 'har', 'jo'. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Rare name fragment, Z-initial

result.description: Fires on the word piece "predict" in the middle of words like unpredictable, unpredictability and predictor, with weaker firing on "comp" in "encompass". Mostly the piece before a suffix such as -able or -ability.
result.label: "predict" word piece mid-word

result.description: Fires on a few unrelated tokens, mostly " since" and " rest" (also " Kind", " as") in academic or encyclopedic text. Members detect "since" and "rest" tokens. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low, so this looks like a loose token set.
result.label: Since / rest token mix

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments inside long, rare academic words (De-ception, anis-otrop-ic, Ali-en-ation, per-ception-al), mostly 'err', 'ception', 'cept', 'ement', where the word is still incomplete. Weak on other pieces.
result.label: Mid-word pieces of rare academic words

result.description: Fires on plural nouns (e.g. industries, countries, authors) that directly follow "various" or "different", ending a category-plural noun phrase. Silent in text without that quantifier-plural construction.
result.label: Plural noun after "various/different"

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'avel' in "wavelength" (and 'cart' in "Descartes"), a word fragment before the rest of the word; predicts continuation like 'ength'. Silent when 'avel' starts the text.
result.label: 'avel' in wavelength / 'cart' in Descartes

result.description: Fires on a period that ends a short title-like heading or name line (e.g. "Resource Allocation Session.", "Engineering.") followed by a paragraph break. It stays silent on periods inside abbreviations or mid-sentence.
result.label: Period ending short heading line

result.description: Fires mainly on "akes" in "high-stakes" (also "stakes" in other uses), with weaker firing on "place", "maintained", "made" after passive/verb constructions. Mostly a "stakes" piece detector with a mixed tail.
result.label: "stakes" word piece 'akes'

result.description: Fires on the noun slot after "depending on the ..." (nature, type, context, application, degree), where a following "of" or a choice-determining noun is expected. It needs a "varies/depends on" construction; the contrast sentence has no such dependence.
result.label: Slot after "depending on the"

result.description: Fires on the word " cycle" (also " cycles") in many contexts: life cycle, water cycle, Carnot cycle, economic cycles. Upstream members are mostly earlier-layer detectors of the same token. It predicts cycle-related continuations like " cycles" and " phases".
result.label: ' cycle' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on ' energy' in "Gibbs free energy" (members detect Gibbs, 'bs', G, thermodynamic). Silent on 'energy' in other contexts like "between energy, pressure". Also weakly on 'ou' in Sturm-Liouville.
result.label: Gibbs free energy 'energy'

result.description: Fires on word pieces that start a longer word and are likely to be continued by a suffix, mainly ' Victor' (before -ian) and 'ad' in 'Leadership'. Predicts continuations such as 'ership', 'io' and 'olph'.
result.label: Victor / Lead- word-start pieces

result.description: Fires on the word right after "mitigate" or "reduce" (e.g. "the", "these risks", "vulnerability"), where the next word is a negative outcome such as effects, risks or damage. It stays silent on "the" after other verbs.
result.label: Object slot after mitigate/reduce

result.description: Fires mostly on " native" before "speaker(s)" in language-learning text, with weaker firing on other modifier nouns like "local", "treatment", "growth". Members are detectors of native/local/target modifiers; predicts a following noun like speaker.
result.label: "native" before speakers, language learning

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments like 'ro' in "grassroots", 'to' in "farm-to-table", 'neum' in "pneumatic", where a word is still incomplete. Silent on 'ro' in other words (assroots, terroirs), so it needs the specific word context.
result.label: Word-piece 'ro' in grassroots

result.description: Fires on function words (the, of, a, first) in explanations of step-by-step procedures or proofs, especially just before "initial/first" step or base case. Weak, mixed evidence; the same tokens elsewhere stay silent.
result.label: Function words before initial step

result.description: Fires on word-piece fragments like 'ru' (Const-ru-ctions, Inter-ru-ptions, dis-ru-ptions) and ' constru' that are mid-word and predict a continuation such as 'ctions' or 'ptions'.
result.label: 'ru' fragment before -ctions/-ptions

result.description: Fires on the 'ut' piece inside "pharmaceutical" (pharmace|ut|ical), including biopharmaceutical. It stays silent on 'ut' in other words such as pollutants and hermeneutic.
result.label: 'ut' in pharmaceutical

result.description: Fires on commas or "and" right after "urbanization" (or similar human-activity items) in lists of drivers of environmental or societal change, predicting the next item such as agriculture or industrialization. Silent on commas after other clause-ending nouns.
result.label: List separator after urbanization

result.description: Peaks mostly on 'umann' in "von Neumann", plus scattered function words like ' between', ' by', ' in' in academic text. Consistency is low and the circuit is diffuse, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: von Neumann 'umann' plus scattered function words

result.description: Fires on the digit '4' as the second digit of a four-digit year starting with 1 (e.g. 1443, 1475, 14th century). It stays silent on '4' in later positions, as in 1764 or 1874, and on '4th' without a leading 1.
result.label: Digit 4 in 14xx years

result.description: Fires on the 'actions' piece of 'reactions' (split as re|actions), mostly in chemistry text such as redox or nuclear reactions. Members are mostly 'actions' detectors at earlier layers.
result.label: 'actions' in re|actions

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' anom' (start of "anomalies") when it is split off as a prefix, mostly in lowercase text about data or computer science. Silent in the all-caps "alIES" variant. Predicts continuations like "aly".
result.label: ' anom' prefix of anomalies

result.description: Fires on the verb ending (-ing, -s) of "reflect" (also "mirror-ed") when the verb is the word being completed, as in "art reflects/reflecting the changing society". Silent on -ing after other verbs like highlight or cook.
result.label: Inflection ending of "reflect"

result.description: Fires on "supply" (or the "ly" ending of "Supply" at the start of a document) in supply-chain text, where the next word is likely "chain". Members are detectors of "supply", "procure-" and related logistics words.
result.label: Supply in supply chain context

result.description: Fires on the word " labor" / " labour" (also "Labor"), mostly as a noun modifier in economics and policy text such as labor markets, costs, demand. Weakly fires on the "labor" start of "laboratory" and "collaboration".
result.label: labor / labour word

result.description: Fires on the token 'b' as a word piece in "Pro-b-ability" (also "probabilistic", "probable"), at a title start. It stays silent on the full word "probability" in running text. Weakly fires on 'b' in other words like turbines.
result.label: 'b' piece in Pro-b-ability

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' coord' when it begins "coordination" (e.g. coordination chemistry, coordination number or complex). Members are mostly detectors of ' coord' and similar prefixes.
result.label: ' coord' start of coordination

result.description: Fires on ' motor' (motor neurons, motor control, motor skills) and on ' well' in "as well as", mostly in neuroscience/anatomy text. Silent on unrelated "movers" contrast text.
result.label: motor / "as well" in neuroscience

result.description: Fires on "while" introducing a participial clause that adds a simultaneous action after a main clause (e.g. "X while also doing Y"). Predicts continuations like also, still, maintain, using, remaining.
result.label: "while" before simultaneous participle

result.description: Fires on word pieces 'ater' (in c-ater-ing, c-ater to) and 'tain' (per-tain-s) where the word is a verb that continues with "to" (cater to, pertain to). Weak on similar pieces like 'ere' in cereals.
result.label: cater/pertain word pieces before "to"

result.description: Fires on connectives (' and', commas, 'the', 'an') inside English grammar explanations, especially in lists of pronoun or preposition types. Silent on many ' and' tokens in similar text, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Connectives in grammar-explanation lists

result.description: Fires on the noun " reach" in marketing and advertising contexts about audience reach (expanding, maximizing, increasing reach). It is quieter on other senses, such as network routes to reach something.
result.label: Audience 'reach' in marketing

result.description: Fires on word-final pieces completing an item in a comma-separated list of nouns (alumin-um, bar-ley, rye, plum), predicting a word-ending piece. Peak tokens are scattered, and it is silent on 'um' in non-list text such as 'optimum'.
result.label: Word endings inside lists

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' obst' (as in "obstacle(s)") mid-sentence, after a determiner like "many" or "an". Silent when it starts a document. Members detect obst/hurdle-like fragments and boost the "acles" continuation.
result.label: ' obst' start of "obstacles"

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'od' in "aerodynamics"/"aerodynamic" (also 'geodetic'), and weakly on other word-internal pieces like 'ps' in "psyche" or 'atom'. Silent on 'od' in "cathodic".
result.label: 'od' inside aerodynamics

result.description: Fires on the word "product"/"products" in several senses: commercial goods, chemical products, and mathematical product (product rule, inner product). It is silent on unrelated text. Predicts suffixes like "-ivity".
result.label: ' product' / ' products' token

result.description: Fires on the token ' Dr' at the start of a line in a list of names (e.g. "Dr. Johnson.¶ Dr. Williams"). Members are mostly ' Dr' detectors from earlier layers. Silent on lists of names without Dr.
result.label: ' Dr' starting list-of-names entry

result.description: Fires on adverb suffixes (-ally, -ically, -ly) that complete a sentence-initial adverb, as in "Generally speaking," "Specifically," "Historically,". Silent on mid-sentence "-ally" such as "culturally and economically". Predicts "speaking"/"though".
result.label: Sentence-initial adverb suffix -ally

result.description: Fires on the token ' growth', mostly after an adjective or noun modifier (sustainable, rapid, exponential, economic). Members are mostly ' growth' detectors; its output favours next words like rates, trajectory, curve.
result.label: ' growth' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word piece " Cons" (capitalized, e.g. Sequential Cons-istency) when it begins a longer word such as "Consistency". It pushes toward continuations like "istent"/"cious".
result.label: " Cons" word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word " stability" (occasionally " convergence") in technical math, engineering and numerical-analysis text, often as the noun after "the" or "ensuring". Predicts property-like next words such as coefficients, properties or rate.
result.label: stability / convergence noun

result.description: Fires on a verb, auxiliary or "of" right after a subject noun or pronoun inside a "why/how/that" clause (e.g. "why we", "why it's", "tools we use... are"). It is silent on some "are" after long subject noun phrases.
result.label: Auxiliary after subject in why-clauses

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'igen' inside 'antigen' (also weaker in 'Indigenous'), mostly in immunology text. It is built from members detecting 'igen'/'ogen' pieces and immune context such as 'foreign' and 'immune'.
result.label: 'igen' in antigen

result.description: Fires on the word " datasets" (also " dataset") in machine-learning and data-science text, especially after "labeled" or "large". Members are mostly detectors of data, dataset and sample words. Weakly fires on "vised" in "Supervised".
result.label: ' datasets' token in ML text

result.description: Fires on the token ' future' (also ' Future'), mostly as a modifier before a noun (predict future market trends, future generations). It predicts nouns like generations, trajectories, directions. Silent on the contrast text, which has no ' future' token.
result.label: ' future' token detector

result.description: Fires on the token " result" (also weaker on resulted/results), mostly as a verb or noun in causal "result in / result from / a result of" phrasing. Predicts suffixes like "ant"/"antly".
result.label: " result" token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on commas inside long lists of abstract nouns (reading, sleeping; reflection, feedback), plus some digits in number strings. Silent on some commas after list-final or clause-ending nouns, so the exact condition is unclear.
result.label: Commas in abstract-noun lists
' external' in externalities
result.description: Fires on ' external' when it begins the word "externalities" (economics: positive/economic externalities). Stays quiet on ' external' in other uses like "external factors" at the start of a text. Predicts the suffix "ities".

result.label: Decade digit in second year of range
result.description: Fires on the decade digit (mostly '7', also 6/8) in "19X0" when it ends a year range, such as "1950s-19[7]0s" or "1962–19[7]0". It stays silent on '7' in other years, such as 1750 or 1874, and in earlier-century dates.

Fires weakly on assorted function words (' to', ' of', ' kept', ' power', ' as') in academic or technical prose, often after participles like "raised", "kept" or "product". Peaks are inconsistent and the target is silent on many identical tokens.
result.label: Scattered function words after participles

result.description: Fires mainly on " noise" in technical contexts like noise levels, noise reduction and signal filtering. It also fires on "aster" in "disaster" and a few odd word pieces. The contrast has "sounds", where it stays silent.
result.label: ' noise' token (acoustic/signal)

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'ocity' (as in "Velocity Components"), plus a few title-like words such as 'laration', ' Missouri' and ' Article' in document-title phrases. It stays silent on 'ocity' in some Vel-ocity contexts. Members are weak, generic and mixed.
result.label: 'ocity' in title-like phrases

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start pieces like ' liter' (literacy), ' orn' (ornamental), ' traject', ' diag', mid-word, where the continuation is a suffix such as 'acy' or 'ament'. Predicts those word completions.
result.label: Word-start fragments: liter-, orn-

result.description: Fires on the degree sign '°' after a number and on 'si' in 'Celsius', i.e. temperature/angle unit tokens. Weak, mixed activity elsewhere (' TO', ' ON'), so the circuit is only partly coherent.
result.label: Degree sign and Celsius 'si'

result.description: Fires on the word piece " citiz" (start of "citizen") in civic-engagement and urban governance text, e.g. "citizen participation" or "citizen science". It predicts the "en" continuation. Weaker on related pieces like "civ" and "en".
result.label: " citiz" start of citizen

result.description: Fires on word pieces like 'ough' in t-ough(er/ness) and 'ild' in m-ild, adjective stems of texture/strength/temperature that take suffixes such as -ness, -er, -ly. Silent on 'ough' in 'dough'.
result.label: Adjective stem pieces: tough, mild

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " demonstr" (occasionally " illustr" or " sign") at the start of demonstrating/demonstrative/demonstration, predicting suffixes like -ating, -atives, -ative. Members are detectors of demonstr/illustr tokens.
result.label: ' demonstr' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' tra' when it starts a word, most strongly in genetics text where it begins "traits" (genetic, dominant, inherited traits). Also fires on other ' tra' starts like trapezo- and trademarks, more weakly.
result.label: ' tra' word-start (traits)

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'histor' inside words like "Prehistoric", where a suffix such as '-ic' is expected next. Members detect similar mid-word pieces (strat-igraph, Paleol-ith, phys-, onom-). Silent on ordinary text.
result.label: 'histor' piece in Prehistoric

result.description: Fires mostly on an opening square bracket " [" (also "|", "...", "(") after a word or operation, as in "operation [" or "+ [". Weaker, scattered hits on other tokens. The circuit is mostly " [" detectors; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Opening square bracket token

result.description: Fires on word pieces completing infrastructure/communication technology terms, mainly "tele-graph", also rail-"ways", road, ads, in lists of transport and communication networks. Predicts network/line/railway-type continuations. Silent on generic transportation prose.
result.label: Telegraph/railways infrastructure word endings

result.description: Fires on verbs meaning "represent/indicate/denote" (representing, represent, indicate, represents) right after a plural subject noun, especially "nodes representing", in technical or explanatory text. It predicts a following description like "whether", "how" or "various".
result.label: represent/indicate verb after subject noun

result.description: Fires on the token " Revolution" as the head of named historical revolutions (French, Russian, Industrial, Scientific, American). It predicts suffixes like "ary" and "ized". Members are mostly detectors of "revolution" tokens.
result.label: Revolution token in named revolutions

result.description: Fires on " both" right after a preposition like "in" or "for", where it begins a paired "both X and Y" phrase (e.g. "important in both theoretical and applied"). It stays quiet on other tokens, including the contrast list of areas.
result.label: "both" after preposition

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'ir' in the middle of words (asp-ir-ations, ch-ir-p, St-ir-ling, resp-ir-atory), plus ' of' in "Internet of Things" and ' ship'. Predicts mid-word continuations like 'voy', 'teen', 'ky'.
result.label: Mid-word 'ir' piece (aspirations, chirp)

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ig' inside "sovereignty" (also in words like pigment, paradigm), predicting a following 'nt'-type continuation. Mostly needs the word-internal 'ig' of these words; occasional weak firing on ' Nash'.
result.label: 'ig' in sovereignty

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'od' in the middle of a word, mostly "mel-od-ies/ic/ious", also par-od-ies and Ge-od-etic. It predicts suffixes like -ic, -ies, -ial. It stays quiet on 'od' at word start or in "embodiment".
result.label: 'od' inside melodies-type words

result.description: Fires on the word " known" itself, as in "known as", "later known as", "is known for", and "all known". Many upstream members are also detectors of " known".
result.label: ' known' token detector

result.description: Fires on auxiliary/passive verbs and connectors (' are', ' be', ' has', ' and') right after a plural or abstract subject noun in business/improvement prose, where a passive participle like "made" or "realized" is expected. Silent on many ' are' tokens.
result.label: Passive auxiliary after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on the word-initial prefix ' dis' (disorder, disaster, disruption, discharge) before the rest of the word is seen. It pushes next-token predictions toward completions like 'order', 'aster', 'rupt' and 'joint'.
result.label: ' dis' prefix before completion

result.description: Fires on ' financial' and on word endings like 'cial' (Finan-cial) and 'ical' (Mathemat-ical) in adjective-like heading words, predicting abstract nouns such as theory, concepts, strategy. Members are mostly financial/cial detectors.
result.label: financial / -cial / -ical adjective endings

result.description: Fires on ' one' used as the generic impersonal pronoun ("one can", "one must") as the subject after a clause-opening comma or conjunction. Silent on ' one' as a numeral or in "each one" and "sometimes one".
result.label: Impersonal pronoun 'one' as subject

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Per' (also 'th') when it begins "Perfect", especially in grammar tense headings like "Past Perfect". Members detect Per/per word-starts that precede a completion such as -fect or -ception.
result.label: ' Per' in "Past Perfect" tenses

result.description: Fires on the token 'ure', both as a word ending (sculpt-ure, expos-ure, adventure) and as a standalone fragment at the start of a heading or sentence. Members are mostly 'ure' token detectors.
result.label: 'ure' token detector

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' Communic' (also ' Integr') after a modifier in list-like topic headings (e.g. "Interpersonal Communication."), predicting a suffix like -ation. Silent on other heading lists.
result.label: Communic- piece in heading lists

result.description: Fires mostly on the split-off piece ' ing' in "ingredient(s)" (tokenized as ' ing' + 'redient'), with weaker firing on scattered tokens like digit '0' and 'etal'. Members are mainly ' ing' detectors in cooking/ingredient contexts.
result.label: ' ing' in ingredient split

result.description: Fires on function words (the, for, a, which) in statistics text about significance levels, hypothesis testing and Type I error, where the next word is likely a statistical term (alpha, Type, Null). Silent on 'the' in general math or definitions.
result.label: Function words in hypothesis-testing text

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece 'ism' completing "realism" (Real+ism), including in art-style contexts. It stays quiet on 'ism' after other stems like modern, Pragmat, connection.
result.label: 'ism' in "realism"

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments like ' vin' (in vinyl), 'div', ' der', where the word continues in a following piece. It mostly peaks on ' vin' before 'yl'. It is silent on ' vin' at the very start of a text.
result.label: ' vin' word-initial fragment (vinyl)

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in abstract academic prose (' economic', ' their', ' differences', ' industrial', 'ino'), often where a noun like a social or economic phenomenon is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent, and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse academic-prose modifier slot

result.description: Fires on varied function words (from, the, of, in) and suffixes like -izing in text about Impressionism and art movements, where the next word is likely an art-related name or term. Silent on 'from' in other art passages, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Function words in Impressionism art text
'yg' piece in hygiene
result.description: Fires on the word piece 'yg' in "hygiene" (h-yg-iene), predicting 'iene' next. Upstream members are mostly 'yg' detectors, including ones from "polygon". It also fires weakly on 'les' in "ecclesiastically".

Fires on function words (the, of, and, from, under) in text about the Russian Revolution and Russian/Soviet empire history, where the next word is likely Russian, Czech or Tsarist. Silent on 'the' in generic century or era phrases.
result.label: Function words in Russian history text

result.description: Fires on the word " marine" (or " Marine") in ocean-life text, such as marine species, animals, habitats, or Marine topic headings. Members are mostly detectors of " Marine" and "aquatic".
result.label: Marine token detector

result.description: Fires on ' one' used as a pronoun standing in for a noun after a determiner or adjective ("the one that", "the first one", "the extended one"). It stays silent on generic "one" as subject ("one must", "one wants") and on "in one place".
result.label: ' one' as noun-substitute pronoun

result.description: Fires on the piece "elling" at the end of "compelling" (comp-elling), predicting persuasion nouns like arguments, reasons, evidence, stories. It stays silent on "elling" in "storytelling".
result.label: "comp|elling" word-piece before arguments

result.description: Fires on words meaning a baseline or yardstick: ' standard' (standardized, standard deviation), ' reference' (reference frame/point), ' benchmark'. Appears in technical or scientific text about measurement and geodesy. Predicts nouns like deviation, frames and points.
result.label: standard / reference / benchmark words

result.description: Fires on the 'ist' piece inside "epistemic/epistemology" (ep-ist-). It stays silent on the suffix 'ist' in words like "consumerist" or "foundationalist". It predicts continuations such as "em".
result.label: 'ist' in epistemic/epistemology

result.description: Fires on the word piece "ver" (and sometimes "val") at the start of words like verbs, verbal, verification, predicting continuations such as "bal", "bs", "itable". Mostly in language/grammar text.
result.label: "ver" word-start piece (verb/verbal)

result.description: Fires on the token " capabilities", typically after a modifier or noun (unique, IDS, spatial mapping, processing). Members are mostly detectors of "capabilities" and similar words (skills, abilities, features). Next-token logits favor "beyond" and "within".
result.label: ' capabilities' token detector

result.description: Fires on mixed word pieces and function words mid-word or in lists (' rev' before 'italize', 'proof' in soundproofing, ' and', commas), where a verb or word continuation is expected. It stays silent on ' rev' in 'revitalization' noun contexts.
result.label: Word-start pieces predicting verb continuations

result.description: Fires on the word piece "it" inside longer words, mainly "facil|it|ator" and also "necess|it|ates". It stays silent on "exhibit" and "prioritizes". It predicts suffixes like -ators, -ates, -ating.
result.label: "it" piece in facilitator

result.description: Fires on the word-initial piece ' t' when it is a split-off start of a longer word, such as tense, tenses, tone, tissue or tune. It pushes towards continuations like 'ense', 'une', 'issues' and 'endencies'.
result.label: Word-initial ' t' fragment

result.description: Fires on the mid-word piece 'it' in "prior-it-ize" (also "emphas", "mand", "advoc" stems) where a verb ending like -ize/-izing is expected next; also on long dash separator runs. Silent on 'it' in other words.
result.label: Word stem before -ize suffix ('prior-it')

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside technical science/engineering terms, mostly 'ator' in actuator/insulator, also 'con' in superconductors, 'zo', 'actu'. Predicts continuations like 'crete', 'duct', 'chan'.
result.label: Technical word fragments (actuator, superconductor)

result.description: Fires on ' and' or commas right after the noun "characters" (e.g. "characters and", "characters, settings") in writing about storytelling and narrative. It stays silent on 'and' after other nouns like pace or dialogue.
result.label: "characters" followed by and/comma

result.description: Fires on ' stream' (and some word-piece fragments like 'al' in 'anomalies') where the word is incomplete or being built, predicting 'line'/'lined' continuations. Mixed with word-fragment detectors; evidence is partly scattered.
result.label: ' stream' / word-piece predicting 'line'

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ao' in "Taoism", mostly at the start of a document. It also fires weakly on a few other mid-word pieces ('imal', 'ros'), where the next token is a suffix such as 'ist' or 'istic'.
result.label: 'ao' in Taoism

result.description: Fires on the word piece "gence" in "emergence", especially "the emergence of ..." in passages about technology or change. Weaker on similar noun endings like "proliferation".
result.label: "emergence" word-ending 'gence'

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words (' to', ' of', ' which') after "flexibility" in the pun sentence, plus the following ' manipulate'. Contrast shows ' to' silent in other settings. Members are scattered, low-share token detectors. The circuit failed, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Function words after 'flexibility of language'

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (conduct, into, circ-uits, explain, engineering) in passages about electrical circuits and electrical engineering. It is silent on 'conduct' in materials or verb contexts, so it needs the electrical-circuits topic.
result.label: Electrical circuits topic context

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (word pieces, 'of', 'in', 'while', periods) in dense, abstract academic-style text, often where text is garbled or run together. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast silences the same '.' token, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in dense academic text

result.description: Fires on function words (' and', ' the', ' with', ' of') mostly after "between the visible X and" or similar coordinated pairs. Silent on many ' and' tokens in lists or other contexts. Members are mixed word-piece detectors; the evidence is weak and the circuit failed.
result.label: Function words in "between X and the"

result.description: Fires on the verb "complicates/complicate" (the 'licates' piece after 'comp'), where a subject makes a following concept or process harder. Weaker on similar verbs like "exacerbates". Predicts an upcoming object noun.
result.label: verb 'complicates' (comp-licates)

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly commas in lists, plus word pieces like "integrated", "reactive", "interference", in technical or scientific text. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak; it stays silent on many commas in other contexts.
result.label: Mixed commas in technical lists

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied function words and mid-phrase tokens (commas, 'and', 'or', 'in', 'to') in abstract expository text. Members are generic and non-discriminative; evidence is thin and the circuit failed.
result.label: Diffuse function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on scattered, mixed tokens (' current', ' throughout', ' are', plural 's', mid-phrase words) in expository text. No coherent trigger or condition is visible. Members are generic token detectors, and the circuit failed on faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mixed tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on varied function words and punctuation (';', ' to', ',', 'and', 'as') within list-like or expository science text, mid-clause. It is silent on some ';' in similar lists, and the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Mixed connectors in expository lists

result.description: Fires on varied function words and continuations (and, of, with, through) in the span right after "biological" or "bio-" in scientific or academic text. It stays quiet on ' and' in other academic contexts without a nearby biological term.
result.label: Words following "biological" in science text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' for', ' of', ' the', ' and', suffixes like 'ades', 'es') in expository prose, with no consistent token or context. Silent on many ' for' cases, so the circuit is diffuse and unreliable.
result.label: Diffuse function-word and suffix firing

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered mid-phrase tokens (word endings like 'ways', 'ages', 'regul', and words like 'include', 'serve', 'which') in academic, expository text. Peaks share no single token, and the circuit failed to reproduce it cleanly.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in expository text
"oring" in "exploring" (pl-oring)
result.description: Fires on the piece "oring" when it completes "exploring" split as "pl"+"oring", often before an object like "the intricacies". It stays silent when the word is split "expl"+"oring", so the particular word split matters.

Fires on " how" right after "similar to" in analogy comparisons ("is similar to how X does Y"). It stays silent on " how" after verbs like "know" or "understand", so it needs the comparison construction.
result.label: "similar to how" analogy

result.description: Fires weakly on function words (' in', ' and', ' of') and nouns like 'changes' or 'process' after "monitor changes" in chemistry measurement text (conductivity, titrations, reaction rates). Silent on ' and' in other topics. Circuit failed and is mixed.
result.label: Monitoring changes in chemical measurements

result.description: Fires on the final piece 'inary' of "interdisciplinary" (also multi-/cross-disciplinary), where a noun like research, collaboration or approach comes next. It was silent in one "interdisciplinary methods" example, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: interdiscipl-'inary' token

result.description: Fires on ' and' (or comma) right after a "too X," clause in the "too high, and… / too fast and you'll…" balance construction, where the following clause gives the consequence. Silent on ordinary list 'and'.
result.label: "too X, and" balance consequence

result.description: Fires on tokens inside the topic phrase after "With regards to / with respect to" (e.g. "the", "Arts", "practice", "istry"), in a document-opening phrase introducing a subject. Silent on "the" after other "to" uses like "led to the".
result.label: Topic phrase after "with regards to"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (the, to, against, their) and 'instrument' in music or skill-related text, but the same ' the' is often silent in similar contexts. Evidence is mixed, the circuit failed, and members are generic.
result.label: Scattered function words in music text

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (commas, 'in', 'the', digits, apostrophes) in the middle of a phrase where a continuation is expected. Evidence is mixed; the contrast shows silence on commas too, with no clear condition.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase function tokens

result.description: Fires in sentences starting "A significant change occurred in the...", peaking on " occurred" and the following " in"/" the" after a document-initial "A significant change" opener. Members are mostly generic token-level hubs; evidence is thin.
result.label: "A significant change occurred in" opener

result.description: Fires on commas and "and"/"or" in a list right after "dendritic cells" or similar items in an enumeration of immune cell types (e.g. "including dendritic cells, macrophages, and B cells"). Silent on "and" in other immune-text contexts.
result.label: List separator after dendritic cells

result.description: Fires on function words (the, in, of, to, that) following technology-related phrasing in abstract essay prose, where "technology" is a likely next word. Silent on the same function words in other contexts. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Function words in technology-themed prose

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word endings (' and', commas, 'ices', 'them') in abstract advice-style prose about balance, harmony, engagement and interpersonal skills. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered tokens in abstract advice prose

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on varied tokens ('apped' in 'untapped', ' industry', ' to', ' available') in business/market text. Members are generic token detectors with no discriminative ones; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Business-text mixed tokens (untapped, industry)

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (' pressure', ' employee', ' to', ' states', ' into', commas) in expository text, mid-sentence where a verb or noun phrase continues. Silent on 'pressure' in physics lists. Members are token-fragment detectors; evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered mid-sentence tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on "stack" and the following "allocation" in computer-science text about stack/heap memory management. Members are mostly "stack" detectors plus memory, thread and data-structure terms. It is silent in unrelated systems text.
result.label: stack allocation in programming text

result.description: Fires on the end of a noun phrase or following punctuation/conjunction after "address(ing) ... disparities/inequalities/issue", i.e. after the object of "address". Silent on commas elsewhere. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Object of "address" (disparities) boundary

result.description: Fires on the verb " exist" (plural subject, as in "free groups exist because"), and sometimes the following " in". Members are mostly detectors of " exist" and its "existential" pieces. The contrast is a text without it.
result.label: verb "exist" detector

result.description: Fires on scattered function-word and word-piece tokens (' and', ' the', 's', ' for') in expository geography, history and culture prose, often mid-phrase before a second item or noun. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed to reproduce the target well.
result.label: Mixed function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the token after "unique"/"distinctive" plus a noun-ish word (propositions of, linguistic, traits, product or service,), where the next word would elaborate the distinguishing properties. Peak tokens are varied; evidence is mixed and low-consistency.
result.label: After unique/distinctive: property slot

result.description: Fires on 'the' or 'of' inside the opening phrase "At the turn of the (century/20th)" at the start of a document. Silent on 'the' after other prepositions like "of the" or "during the". Members are mostly generic 'the' detectors.
result.label: "At the turn of the" opener

result.description: Fires on the open parenthesis after a technical term or multi-word name, where an abbreviation or symbol like (PMF), (CAD), (P) is likely to follow. Silent on parentheses that start ordinary asides like "(or ...)".
result.label: Parenthesis introducing abbreviation
Subject pronoun after where/how clause
result.description: Fires on subject pronouns (' they', ' you', ' we') and 'as' inside an embedded clause after "where", "how" or "as much about", as in "stay where they are". It stays silent on 'they' after a colon, semicolon or main-clause verb.

Fires on transitive verbs like promote, cause, allows, assess, help, right after a modal or "to" with a subject noun phrase, where an object noun comes next. Silent on "promote" after "also" or a comma. Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Verb after modal predicting object

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit: target peaks on varied function words (' where', ' of', ' with', ' since', ' secure') and document start, in abstract expository text. It is silent on some ' where' cases, and members are diffuse token detectors, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed function-word peaks, diffuse circuit

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' en' in "automatic enrollment" (after "automatic"), where it begins a word like enrollment. Silent on ' en' in other words such as enrich, enhanced, enforce, encompasses.
result.label: ' en' in "automatic enrollment"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' we', ' expl', ' this', 'of') inside "as we move forward / progress further" style sentences about exploring or understanding a field. Silent on ' we' in other clauses such as "perhaps we should" or "as we look".
result.label: "We move forward" exploration phrasing

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly commas but also ' when', ' as', ' the' and word pieces, in scientific or technical text. The contrast shows commas in similar text staying silent, so the condition isn't clear. The circuit fails and its members are generic.
result.label: Scattered commas in technical text

result.description: Fires weakly on assorted function words and mid-phrase tokens (' and', ' their', ' these', ' essential', ' been') in expository academic text, where a following noun or continuation is expected. No clear single token or construction; the circuit is a weak, low-faithfulness fit.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires mostly on " in" right after "changes" (changes in Earth's / the market / consumer behavior), plus a few other tokens. The contrast shows the same "changes in" also staying silent, so the extra condition is unclear. The circuit failed its faithfulness check.
result.label: "in" after "changes"

result.description: Fires on word pieces inside multi-word topic or course-name list items (e.g. "Biomedical Ethics", "Financial Technology", "IoT") in list-like headings separated by paragraph breaks. Silent on some "ics" endings like "Mathematics". Weak, mixed evidence.
result.label: Topic-title word pieces in lists

result.description: Fires on function words (that, the, as, such as) right after metrics/measurement language (KPIs, measure, indicators), where a measured quantity is about to be named. Predicts metric/benchmark-type words. Silent on 'that' after generic business insights.
result.label: Function words after metrics/measurement talk

result.description: Fires on scattered punctuation and function words (commas, "),", "and", "of", "to") in abstract expository lists and business or academic prose. No dominant token, and it is silent on many commas. The circuit failed and the evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered punctuation in expository lists

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied mid-phrase tokens (adverbs, conjunctions, word pieces) in abstract academic prose, often where a continuation is expected. Peaks are scattered and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on the final '4' of "BB84" (also the '9' in a year like 1984), in quantum cryptography text. It is silent on '4' in IP v4 or a section number "4.", so it needs the BB84 name context.
result.label: BB84 protocol name final digit

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and word pieces (' and', '-', ' the', ',', ' of') in technical or academic prose, mid-list or mid-phrase. Peaks are scattered with low consistency, and the members are generic token detectors. No clear single role.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic text

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (' different', ' to', ' (', ',', 'by', word pieces) in expository technical text. No consistent token or context; the circuit failed and members are generic. Logits favor science/technical words weakly.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires mostly on ' tort' in legal text ("modern English tort law"), with a few weaker hits on word pieces like 'ation' in "Quadratic Equation". Supported by legal and legislation-related upstream members. The circuit failed faithfulness, so the picture is partial.
result.label: ' tort' in legal text

result.description: Fires mostly on "rop" in "crop" and on "," or " and" following crop-related terms in agricultural/biotech text (crop efficiency, crop diversification and). Mixed peaks and low consistency; evidence is weak.
result.label: crop word piece and following connectives

result.description: Fires on the subject slot right after a sentence-initial "using X," clause: ' it', ' one', or agent nouns like policymakers/investors/readers (-ers). It stays silent on "researchers" in object position.
result.label: Subject after "using X," clause

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' assess' (assessment/assessing), mostly in environmental, educational or technical assessment tool contexts. It stays quiet on 'assess' in business risk-assessment text. Members are 'assess' detectors that push 'ment'.
result.label: ' assess' word piece, non-business

result.description: Fires on ' adapt' when it begins "adaptive" right after "such as" or "like" in a list of technologies. It stays silent on the verb "adapt to", as in "models that adapt to changing conditions".
result.label: ' adapt' in "such as adaptive"

result.description: Fires on function words (and, of, on, with) or a repeated "Computer" right after "computer science/engineering" context, where the next word is likely a field term like science or engineering. Silent on 'and' in other lists.
result.label: Function words after computer-science phrases

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on ' analysis' (notably after "error"), plus ' shape', ' to', ' can', ' aid'. It stays silent on "analysis" after thorough/critical/comprehensive. Members are generic and non-discriminative; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered 'analysis' after 'error'

result.description: Fires on " the" (also "like", " today") right after a sentence-ending period followed by "like", as in ".like the idealized shape". Silent on ordinary " the" mid-sentence after verbs or prepositions. Members are mostly generic token detectors.
result.label: "like the" after a period

result.description: Fires on function words that introduce an example or list item, like "such as", "like", "including", "being the", often before a named example. It is inconsistent, and the same "as" is silent in other contexts. The circuit is weak and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Example-introducing connectives (such as)

result.description: Fires on commas, "of", "that", "who" right after a noun naming an ancient civilization (Indus Valley Civilization, Sumerians, Hittites), where a descriptive clause or appositive follows. Silent on commas after similar nouns in other settings.
result.label: Punctuation after ancient civilization names

result.description: Fires on commas and ' and' inside lists of abstract nouns (security, transaction management, and logging; risk assessment, business continuity, and...), at the join before the next list item. Evidence is mixed: it is silent on similar list 'and's, so the circuit is weak.
result.label: Abstract-noun list separators

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, 'is', 'found', digits, word pieces) in expository science and food text, mid-phrase. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so no clear trigger or condition emerges.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase expository tokens

result.description: Fires on the word right after "riding" (on, a, the) inside simile-style "it's like riding..." phrases comparing an abstract process to an activity. Silent on similar "like walking on a" contexts, so the condition is narrow and unclear.
result.label: Function word after "like riding"

result.description: Fires on function words (' are', ' and', ' as', ' that') right after the subject "principles" (or similar), e.g. "principles and concepts", "principles serve as". Predicts law/apply-type continuations. Silent on ' are' after other subjects.
result.label: Function words after "principles"

result.description: Fires on connective function words (' and', ',', ' to', ' who', ' as') in abstract expository prose about organizations, processes or ideas, where a list or continuation follows. It stays silent on the same ' and' in many similar contexts, so the condition is unclear. The circuit failed.
result.label: Connectives in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the end of the first noun phrase after "balance" (e.g. "risks and benefits", "new products", "responsibilities"), where a "with/between" contrast is expected next. Silent on the same tokens elsewhere, such as "dialogue".
result.label: Noun ending balance-X phrase

result.description: Fires on connectives or continuation tokens (" and", ",", " in", "innovation") right after "creativity" or "foster creativity" lists. Silent on " and" in other contexts, so it needs the creativity context. Members detect "cre-ativity".
result.label: Token after "creativity" in lists

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function tokens, mostly commas in lists of items or steps (e.g. "approval, closure, inspection"), plus "and", "that", "two". Evidence is mixed. The circuit failed and members are diffuse.
result.label: Commas in lists, mixed function words

result.description: Fires on tokens shortly after the verb "fill" (e.g. "fill the", "fill an atom", "fill in", dough after "filling an empty"), at varied positions in the phrase. Fill-detector members feed it. It stays silent on ordinary " and" without "fill" earlier.
result.label: Tokens following the verb "fill"

result.description: Fires on tokens in the predicate after the modal "must" (e.g. "must be", "must convey ... and", "must have ...,"), where a requirement is being listed. Silent on "can be" or "may be", so it needs "must".
result.label: Continuation after "must" requirements

result.description: Weak, mixed layer-6 attention latent peaking on varied tokens (' pain' in paints, 'ors' in transistors, ' increased', '0' in a year) where a word is part of a combination or mixing context. Circuit failed, so evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed tokens in combining contexts

result.description: Fires on ' of' after an abstract action or process noun (detection, identification, creation of ...), in technical or academic text. It stays silent on some 'of' after similar nouns like development, study, exploration, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: ' of' after process nouns

result.description: Fires on an opening quote mark (or comma) that follows a quoted word in a list of quoted example words or markers, such as "well," "so," in linguistics text. It stays quiet on a quote that opens a single example after "such as".
result.label: Quote mark in quoted-example lists

result.description: Fires on " mark" and the following hyphen in the "mark-and-sweep" garbage collection algorithm name. It stays silent on hyphens in other compounds. Weak activation on "mark" in market/marketing words.
result.label: mark-and-sweep garbage collection
' with' after a noun or comma
result.description: Fires on the word ' with' when it follows a noun or a comma and introduces an added element, as in "X, with a career…" or "in the 1960s with the emergence…". It stays silent on some ' with' tokens after clauses, and the contrast doesn't show why.

Fires on scattered function words (' your', ' be', ' like', ' are', ' while') in second-person, advice-style text, often after a subject or modal. It stays silent on some ' your' tokens after prepositions or verbs. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered 'your'/'be' in second-person text

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on commas, "and", and "to" after a noun or verb like "seeking", often where a list or continuation follows. Contrast commas in other lists stay silent. Members are mostly generic token detectors; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered commas, 'and', 'to' connectors

result.description: Diffuse attention-based target peaking on assorted tokens (' implicitly', ' and', ' the', ' of', word-start pieces) in abstract academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent and members are generic list/word-piece detectors; the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse mixed function-word peaks

result.description: Fires on 'also', 'commonly', 'known' or 'often' right after a comma following a subject noun at the start of a text, introducing an alias ("X, also known as..."). Silent on 'also' used as a plain adverb mid-clause.
result.label: Alias introducer: ", also known as"

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on scattered tokens such as ' sometimes', ' Computer', ' in' and ' for' in computing or technical prose. Members are generic and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in technical prose

result.description: Fires on the word right after "understand" (or "know"), e.g. "understand the", "understand not", "understand their". It is an attention-based latent that marks the object slot of the verb. The peak token itself varies.
result.label: Word after "understand"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ending a noun phrase in a list or coordination (comma, "or", plural endings, "claims", "efforts"), mostly in expository text about weather, risk and abstract topics. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Noun-phrase end in lists

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly the article ' a'/' an' (also 'B', 'even'), where a noun phrase is expected next. It is silent on many other ' a' tokens. Members are mostly generic early-layer 'a' detectors, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Scattered article 'a' before noun

result.description: Fires mostly on sentence-ending periods in abstract expository prose, sometimes at the start of the next sentence or on words like "as" or "to". It stays silent on many other periods, and the evidence doesn't show what separates them.
result.label: Sentence-final period in expository prose

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' and', ' en', 'ization', ' modification') in formal scientific or expository prose, especially ' and' inside noun-phrase coordination. It stays silent on ' and' after commas in casual, metaphorical text. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: 'and' in formal expository coordination

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (' in', ' the', digits, ' it') in abstract expository prose about culture, history or art. Peaks are inconsistent and the same ' in' is silent elsewhere. Members are generic and the circuit failed, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose
