result.description: Fires on ' and' (also ' as', ' or') in lists of social-science factors, e.g. "socio-cultural developments, and" before the final item. Silent on similar list-final 'and' in other contexts; the circuit is weak and the condition is unclear.
result.label: List-final 'and' in socio-cultural lists

result.description: Fires on scattered function tokens (commas, "and", "is", "of", "are", "can") inside expository lists and noun-phrase sequences in formal or technical prose. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak. Silent on some commas in similar lists.
result.label: Commas and function words in lists

result.description: Fires on the prepositions ' in' and ' into' (also weakly ' to', ' with') after a noun, notably in title-like phrases such as "The Role of Technology in History" and "Idioms in Education". Silent on some ' into' cases such as "insight into".
result.label: Preposition 'in'/'into' after noun

result.description: Fires on the token inside or right after a list item following "include/includes" (e.g. "include more", "include pian-os", "include real-time"), where an enumerated item is being introduced. Peak tokens vary; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Items within "include" lists

result.description: Fires at varied positions right after a "X has been an essential/integral component/element/part of ..." framing, on words continuing the phrase (life, for, the, inter-, element). Peak tokens are mixed, and it stays silent on some 'inter' tokens in similar sentences.
result.label: Essential-component-of phrase continuation

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on varied noun or suffix tokens (' structure', 'ing', ' instrument', ' delete') that end a phrase, often after a noun modifier. It stays silent on ' structure' in other contexts. Evidence is thin and the members are generic.
result.label: Mixed phrase-final tokens, structure/-ing

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (many, product, projects, 'ing', ' of') in economics and finance text. Members are mostly economy and finance detectors. The peak tokens are inconsistent, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: Finance/economics text, varied tokens

result.description: Peaks scatter across unrelated tokens (word pieces like 'ide' in fluoride, ' gas', ' of', ' the', ' as'), mostly mid-word or within noun phrases in technical text. Consistency is low and the circuit fails faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on "ival" in "differential survival" and on ")," closing a parenthetical in a list, just before "reproduction". It stays silent on "ival" in plain "survival" without the "differential" before it. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: differential survival / list-closing paren
Connector words after abstract nouns
result.description: Fires on connective function words and dashes (through, from, to, —) that link a clause to a following elaboration, in abstract academic or art prose. Silent on 'through' after motion verbs. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.

Weak, mixed target peaking on varied tokens ('ph' in allophones, ' from', ' software', ' data', ' and'). It is silent on 'ph' in polyphonic. Members are mostly generic token detectors and list-start markers; evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed tokens, 'ph' in allophones

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (periods, "to", "on", "providing", "-oring") in expository text about tailoring or structuring a process or approach, where a verb or noun phrase describing a method or step is expected next. Peaks are inconsistent. The same period token is often silent.
result.label: Process/method description, varied tokens

result.description: Fires on connective or function tokens (' and', ' as', ' with', ',', '-') inside abstract lists or coordinated phrases in data, research and business text. Stays silent on many ' and' tokens, and the cause is unclear. Weak circuit.
result.label: Connectives in abstract data-topic lists

result.description: Fires on words and punctuation inside a list of requirements right after "the need/necessity/demand for" (e.g. "need to create robust, efficient, and"). It is silent on ordinary "and" elsewhere. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Tokens after "need for" phrases

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after "sense" in "sense of X" (our sense of self-worth, sense of harmony). Silent on ' of' after other nouns like components, context, density, personality.
result.label: ' of' after "sense"

result.description: Fires on a comma or "and" right after the word "peace" (peace, stability, and… / peace and security), in a list of goals. Silent on commas after other nouns. Members detect "peace"/"peaceful" plus generic comma/and list positions.
result.label: Comma/and after "peace" in lists

result.description: Fires on the pieces of "avant-garde" (mainly "gar", also "de" and the hyphen) when the word is spelled out. It stays quiet on "gar" in other words such as "Edgar". Early members detect " avant" and the hyphen.
result.label: avant-garde word pieces

result.description: Fires weakly on varied connective or mid-phrase tokens (' and', ' with', 'ization', ' quality', ' uses') in abstract expository text about music, soil, or sodium. Mixed peaks and a failed circuit; the contrast does not clearly show what separates it from silent ' and'.
result.label: Mixed connectives in expository text

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit firing on scattered function and adjective tokens (' be', ' are', ' political', ' financial', "'"). Silent on ' be' after 'can' in other contexts; members are mostly generic rare-token detectors. Evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered be/are/political tokens

result.description: Fires on "of" (and word pieces like -ical, -ological) right after quality/reliability/accuracy/authenticity-type nouns, where a scientific or analytic object comes next. It stays quiet on "of" after "use", "field", "application".
result.label: "of" after quality/reliability nouns

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking mostly on ' of' after abstract nouns (collection of, breakdown of), plus scattered tokens like ' water', 'ing', ' both'. Silent on many other ' of' contexts; the circuit failed and members are diffuse, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered ' of' after nouns (weak)

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words (' the', ' for', ' and', ' of') and word pieces in abstract expository prose, often after 'of' or a verb. The same ' the' often stays silent, and the evidence doesn't show why. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "importance" or "significance" (e.g. "the importance of X"). It is silent on some other "importance of" cases, so the rule is not fully clear. Upstream members detect importance/significance words and "of".
result.label: "of" after importance/significance

result.description: Fires on virus- and bacteria-related word pieces (' vir', 'b'/'acter', 'and') in microbiology and genetics text, e.g. "viruses", "bacteria", "viral vector". Silent on general genetics text without these microbe words.
result.label: Virus and bacteria word pieces

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' and', ' of', ' in', 'us') in academic or expository text, often mid-list or after a noun in a coordinated phrase. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness; the contrast shows no clear condition.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on tokens in and right after the name Mendeleev (the "le" piece, "'s", " in") in chemistry/atomic-science text. It stays silent on "'s" after other scientists' names, so it seems tied to Mendeleev.
result.label: Mendeleev name continuation tokens

result.description: Fires on the 'ing' piece in 'plementing' (implementing), after the 'plement' fragment. It stays silent on 'ing' in other words like maintaining, proofing, employing. Members include a 'plement' detector and implementation-related members.
result.label: 'ing' in 'plementing'

result.description: Fires on "The" when it begins a title of a work (show, play, epic, publication) inside quotes or a list of titles, e.g. 'The Shadow', "The Importance of…". It stays silent on ordinary running text.
result.label: "The" starting a work title

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' as', ' in', ' of', ' for', 'Q') in technical or academic text. Peaks are inconsistent, and ' as' is silent in "such as" in the contrast. The evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in technical text

result.description: Fires on the word " Media" (also " media"), mostly as a heading at the start of a line or document, like "Media Strategy" or "Media Evaluation" in marketing-plan outlines. It stays silent on other headings such as "Public" in the contrast.
result.label: Media as a heading word

result.description: Fires on the pieces of "co-stimulatory signals/molecules" in immunology text: "atory" within co-stimul-atory, then " signals" or "molecules" right after it. It stays silent on " signals" in other immune contexts without "co-stimulatory".
result.label: co-stimulatory signals/molecules

result.description: Fires mostly on commas (also "ate", "and") separating items in a list of verb phrases or abstract nouns about promoting collaboration, innovation, or discourse. Silent on commas in some similar lists of virtues, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Commas in abstract promotion lists

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on varied tokens in technical or math text (' in', ' within', 'uro', 'auss', ' attached'), often a word right after a noun, before a relative "which". Members are generic and non-discriminative; the evidence is unclear.
result.label: Mixed technical-text tokens, unclear
' such' after "applications/fields"
result.description: Fires on ' such' (as in "such as") right after a noun like "fields" or "applications" in phrases like "important in fields such as". It is quieter after other nouns such as concepts, methods or mechanisms.

Fires mostly on " is" (also " of") after a quoted nickname like "The God Particle," before a predicate such as "an essential element". Silent on " is" after plain subjects like "The bottom quark". Members are diffuse and low-specificity, and the circuit failed.
result.label: " is" after quoted nickname appositive

result.description: Fires mostly on ' health' (also ' gold', 'lic', 'ably', ' for') after a preposition like 'in' in policy/economics text, but stays silent on some ' health' cases such as 'financial health'. Circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: ' health' after 'in' in policy text

result.description: Fires on the word right after "Dendritic" at the start of a document (" cells", " polym", " structure"). It stays silent on " cells" after other words like "T cells" or "antigen-presenting cells". Members are mostly generic word-piece detectors.
result.label: Noun after "Dendritic" at start

result.description: Fires weakly on varied tokens inside lists or coordinated noun phrases (commas, "and", "in", nouns like management/practices) in expository text. The pattern is diffuse and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the trigger is not clear.
result.label: Diffuse list and coordination positions

result.description: Fires on function words like " to", " for", " be" after "essential/crucial/important (for X)" in writing-advice and grammar text, but the same " to" often stays silent in similar contexts. The circuit is diffuse and unfaithful.
result.label: Infinitive 'to' after importance phrases

result.description: Fires on 'of', 'from' or '(' right after "life cycle" / "lifecycle" (assessment) phrases, in sustainability and engineering text. Silent on 'of' after other nouns like "analysis of" or "impact of".
result.label: 'of' after life cycle

result.description: Fires on conjunctions (' and', ' or', commas) and some word pieces in technical science/ML text (biology, neural networks, data). It is silent on many ' and' tokens in general text, so the pattern is mixed and the condition is unclear.
result.label: Conjunctions in technical science text

result.description: Fires on " Capital" in the title "The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism", just before "ism". Members include Luther and Church detectors, suggesting Protestant/religion context supports it.
result.label: Capital in Spirit of Capitalism

result.description: Fires on varied function and filler words (and, of, an, is, economic) in text about law, regulation and economics, apparently preparing a legal or economic term next. Members detect legal and financial word pieces. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Legal/economic text, varied function words

result.description: Fires on commas separating items in a list of fields, disciplines or topics (e.g. "mathematics, chemistry, ..."), mid-list after a noun. It stays quiet on commas after a single term like "science," that is not part of an enumeration.
result.label: Comma in list of fields

result.description: Fires on the function word or verb right after the subject "incentives" (are, and, be, play, like), in essays about incentives. It stays quiet on 'are' after other subjects such as ethics or frameworks. Logits favour reward/pay words.
result.label: Word after "incentives" subject

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention-layer target firing on mixed tokens (' the', ' of', ' complex', ' like') mostly after verbs like "simplifying" or "understanding" in technical text. Members are mostly word-piece detectors; the evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Diffuse function words after technical verbs

result.description: Fires on the word or word piece right after "standardized", "unified" or "structured" (catalog-ing, financial, comma, -ess, -ations). It marks the noun slot in a standardization phrase. Logits are mixed and unclear.
result.label: Word after standardized/unified

result.description: Weak, diffuse attention-layer target firing on scattered tokens (' the', ' of', ' becomes', ' to', word pieces), often inside title-like or named phrases such as "Land of the Free". The circuit failed faithfulness; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Diffuse function-word and piece firing

result.description: Fires on math notation tokens like parentheses, '=' and the start of the right-hand side in text describing "the general form" of a function or equation. Peaks are scattered and weak; the same '=' stays silent in other equation contexts.
result.label: Math notation after "general form"

result.description: Fires on the final piece of an acronym such as TCR or BCR, the 'R' or 'TC' after "T cell receptor (" in immunology text. Silent on 'R' in a different context (virus-infected (TCR) infr...). Members are mixed acronym and generic detectors.
result.label: Receptor acronym TCR/BCR piece

result.description: Fires on ' logical' (also 'ic' in 'epistemic') in a specific abstract philosophy/logic passage, e.g. after "categorical" in text on deductive reasoning. Silent on ' logical' in other contexts. Circuit is weak and diffuse, with philosophy-themed members.
result.label: ' logical' after 'categorical' in philosophy

result.description: Fires on the verb " rely" right after a plural subject, as in "Artists rely heavily on...". Weaker on related forms like "relied" and "depend". Members detect rely/depend/reliance words that predict "on" or "heavily".
result.label: ' rely' verb before 'on'

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' imag' (imaging, imagery, imaginary), where the next piece completes the word. Upstream members are mostly ' imag' token detectors across layers, plus a few detectors of other word-start pieces such as fa, l, Spect.
result.label: ' imag' word-start piece

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target firing on scattered function words (' is', ' more', ' as', ' them') in culinary or knife-related text. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit fails faithfulness; members are generic and non-specific.
result.label: Scattered function words, culinary text

result.description: Fires on adjectives of care and rigor (meticul-ous, careful, proper, thorough) right before a noun like attention, planning, or adherence. Members detect careful/thorough/rigorous words. Likely predicts nouns of process.
result.label: Careful/meticulous adjective before process noun

result.description: Fires on " of" right after a quality-type noun (quality, depth, nuance, complexity, clarity) following "elevate/enhance/enrich" in abstract, essay-like text. Silent on " of" after other nouns, such as "power of" or "utilization of".
result.label: " of" after elevate-the-quality nouns

result.description: Fires on conjunctions and function words (' and', ' or', ' but', ' in') after a clause or list item, plus ' Mov' in ARIMA. Silent on many ' and' tokens in other contexts. Weak, low-faithfulness circuit; condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered conjunctions after list items

result.description: Fires on commas (also 'and', 'or') separating items in a list of examples, e.g. foods, sauces, materials, after "such as" or "including". Silent on commas in ordinary clauses or non-list uses.
result.label: List-item separators in example lists
Mid-term word-piece continuation in technical terms
result.description: Fires on scattered tokens in the middle of multi-piece technical terms or names (Kaplan-Meier, VR, nonparametric, ray tracing), where a continuation is expected. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit failed and is weak evidence.

Fires on varied tokens inside business/legal-style expository lists and noun phrases (' and', ' or', ' legal', 'atives' in 'initiatives'), but stays silent on 'atives' in 'narratives'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Business/legal list connectives and word pieces
" of" after "success" at document start
result.description: Fires on " of" right after "The success" at the very start of a document. It stays quiet on " of" after other nouns such as importance, quality, aspect or interaction. Members mostly detect "success" and its variants.

Fires on varied tokens (verbs, word pieces, commas, 'the') mid-sentence in technical or scientific text about genetics, clustering and maps, where a technical noun is expected next. The peak token is not consistent, and the same 'the' stays silent in other places.
result.label: Technical text mid-phrase, varied tokens

result.description: Fires on the last piece of a word or compound right after "entrenched", mostly "service" in "fee-for-service" and suffixes like "-ist" in "mercantilist". Evidence is thin and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Word end after "entrenched" (fee-for-service)

result.description: Fires weakly on varied tokens in one passage about weather and humanity's "thirst for"/"quest to understand", mostly on ' for', ' patterns', ' understand'. Silent on other ' for' uses. Members are diffuse and the circuit fails, so evidence is thin.
result.label: Thirst/quest for understanding phrasing

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target peaking on varied tokens (' in', ' and', ' to', ' need', ' new') in abstract academic/scientific prose, mid-phrase after a noun or verb. Fires inconsistently and stays silent on some ' in' cases; evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires mostly on ' with' after a comma that opens a trailing absolute clause ("culture, with its..."), in descriptive essay-like text; also occasionally on '.' or ' the'. Silent on some ' with' in similar contexts, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Comma-led ' with' clause opener

result.description: Fires weakly on varied tokens ending a noun phrase, often plural abstract nouns like 'points', 'approaches', 'techniques', 'qualities', or 'FS'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed, so the pattern is not clear.
result.label: Plural method/viewpoint nouns, mixed

result.description: Fires on word pieces or nouns inside long comma-separated lists of abstract process nouns (dissemination, utilization, maintenance, facilitation), mostly mid-word or on list items. Members are list-comma and "etc"-style list detectors.
result.label: Items in abstract noun lists

result.description: Diffuse attention-layer target firing on scattered tokens (word endings, prepositions like for/in/or/to, 'on', 'its') mid-sentence in formal prose. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and unfaithful, so no clear meaning emerges.
result.label: Diffuse mid-sentence function-word latent

result.description: Fires on the token " breaks" (plural noun) in text about narrative or writing pauses, such as "narrative breaks serve as...". Members detect break/breaks/breaking tokens. Weak on other break- pieces. Silent on contrast text without it.
result.label: "breaks" as narrative pauses

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (function words, word pieces, nouns) in abstract academic prose, mid-phrase where a noun or technical term is expected next. Peak tokens are inconsistent and the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase academic prose

result.description: Weak, mixed circuit firing on scattered function words (' and', ' the', ' its', ' makes', ' study') in academic or expository text. Members are generic token detectors and the contrast shows no clear separating condition; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered function words, unclear

result.description: Fires on function words (' a', ' the', ' to', ' in') right after a sentence subject like "combination of X and Y" or "amalgamation", i.e. the verb-then-object slot after a combining/integration noun. Silent on ' a' in other contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function word after 'combination' subject

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (word pieces like 'ion', 'ary', 'ful', and ' resource', ' to') in definitional passages about access control and abstract concepts. Peaks are scattered and the members are mostly generic token detectors, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens in definitions

result.description: Fires on the suffix "ness" completing "consciousness" (and weakly on " conscious" before it) in philosophy-of-mind text. It stays silent on "ness" in other words like "directedness" or "richness".
result.label: "ness" in "consciousness"

result.description: Fires on tokens (' the', word pieces like -ives, -istic, -ions) that complete the object of "setting"/"set" (goals, objectives, the tone, the stage). It stays silent on 'the' after other verbs like "incorporate" or "into".
result.label: Object slot after "setting"

result.description: Fires diffusely on varied function words and mid-phrase tokens (and, that, their, -ling) in technical or academic text on math and science. Peaks are inconsistent, and the circuit is low-faithfulness with no discriminative members.
result.label: Diffuse technical-text function words

result.description: Fires on tokens within text about prime numbers and number-theory conjectures (Twin Primes, "Prime Conjecture", "prime numbers", "are"), but stays silent on "conjecture" in other contexts like the Poincaré Conjecture. Needs the prime-number topic.
result.label: Prime number theory text

result.description: Fires on " the" (occasionally " of" or " that") right after "second half of" or "latter half of", where a century or decade comes next. It stays silent on "of the" after other nouns such as "dawn of" or "movements of".
result.label: "the" after "second half of"

result.description: Fires on the verbs of giving or taking in acid-base and redox chemistry, mainly 'ate' in "donate" and ' accept' after "bases", plus related words like 'gains' and 'pairs'. It stays silent on 'ate' in "conjugate" or "consolidate".
result.label: Donate/accept in acid-base chemistry

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (word pieces, "of", "as", "both") inside abstract academic sentences of the form "how X can contribute to / function as / affect Y". Peaks are scattered; the circuit seems to track that "how ... verb" frame.
result.label: Abstract "how X can affect Y" frame

result.description: Fires on tokens right after the word "thematic" (narrative, map, elements, and, development), i.e. the word or piece following "thematic". It stays silent on " elements" after "these" or "narrative", so it needs the preceding "thematic".
result.label: Token following "thematic"

result.description: Fires on the piece 'our' inside "flour"/"flourish" (fl+our), mostly in "flourished/flourishing". Members are detectors of this 'our' after 'fl'. Predicts continuations like -ishing/-ished.
result.label: 'our' in flour/flourish

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (commas, 'ived', ' with', word endings) inside lists of abstract nouns in academic or social-science prose, such as legal or social frameworks. Mixed peaks and a failed circuit; the condition is unclear.
result.label: List-like academic prose, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on " and" (also " or") joining two nouns in a pair of parallel items, strongest in "tokamaks and stellarators" in fusion text. Silent on "and" ending longer lists or joining clauses.
result.label: "and" joining two paired nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (suffix 'ing', 'and', 'or', 'the', 'that') mostly inside paired or coordinated phrases like "opportunities and challenges" or "young and old". Peaks are inconsistent; the circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Coordination slots in paired phrases

result.description: Fires on varied tokens ending a noun phrase in technical text (enterprises, browsers, language, conductors, 'a', 'in'), often after "within/between/inside". Members suggest predicting a context or setting noun. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Technical phrase-end before context noun

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (has, have, that, a, a verb after a subject) right after a long abstract subject noun phrase about the influence of crafts, math or science, where a predicate about impact is expected. Silent on relative 'that' after a noun.
result.label: Predicate slot after abstract subject

result.description: Fires on " but" or " also" in the "not only X but also Y" correlative construction, at the second half after the first clause. It stays silent on "but" in other uses, such as plain contrastive "but" after a comma.
result.label: "not only... but also" second half

result.description: Fires on function words (and, of, an, a, is) right after the word "basis" in linear algebra text, e.g. "A basis is an...", "basis and the concept". Silent on "and" in other math contexts without "basis" just before.
result.label: Function words after "basis" (linear algebra)

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens, such as 'and', commas, 'our' and word pieces, usually where a new word or word continuation is expected. Peaks are mixed and the circuit failed. The contrast shows 'and' ending lists is silent.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase continuation tokens

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (of, to, between, it, 's) in abstract expository text about science, economics and society. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' and', commas, ' the', ' to') and word pieces in expository lists and technical prose, but stays silent on ' and' ending a comma-separated list. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Mixed connectives in expository prose
'ception' in "deception"
result.description: Fires on the piece 'ception' when it completes the word "deception" (de|ception). It stays silent on 'ception' in other words like "preconceptions", where members detecting 'de' plus the piece matter.

Fires on the first token (often ' the', ' sust', ' a', ' N') right after "prioritizes" or "emphasizes" near the start of a document, where the next word is the thing being prioritized. Silent on ' the' after other verbs or words.
result.label: Object after prioritizes/emphasizes

result.description: Fires on ' fixed' (also arbitrary, limited, absolute) when it follows a negation like "is not", as in "meaning is not fixed". Members detect negation words and static/limited adjectives, in abstract philosophical or conceptual text.
result.label: "not fixed" after negation

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered tokens (function words like ' to', ' of', ' the', plus word pieces) in academic-style text, with no consistent token or context. The contrast shows ' to' silent in many places. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Scattered function-word positions, unclear

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target peaking on plural-person or quantifier words like "individuals", "all", "them", "users", and occasionally mid-word pieces. Members are generic token detectors; evidence is thin and the circuit failed.
result.label: Plural people/quantifier words (weak)

result.description: Fires on ' Fre' as the first piece of the surname "Freire" after "Paulo", in education-theorist lists. Silent on ' Fre' starting "Freeman" in a list of famous people. Members are mostly education/teaching topic and word-piece detectors.
result.label: Fre in Paulo Freire

result.description: Fires on connectors like " even", " (", " and", " sometimes" right after "dozens (or/and)", where a larger quantity ("thousands", "millions") is about to be given. Silent on " even" in other uses.
result.label: Escalation after "dozens" toward thousands

result.description: Fires on ' into', ' among', ' are' and similar words right after a "if n items are distributed/placed" clause in pigeonhole-principle-style combinatorics statements. Silent on ' into' in other uses (divide into, insight into).
result.label: Pigeonhole distribution: items placed into/among

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (' in', ' by', ' rather', ' to', ' another') that follow a verb or participle and introduce a prepositional or contrastive phrase, in abstract expository text. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast offers no clear rule.
result.label: Scattered prepositions after verbs

result.description: Fires after "create/foster an environment" (or "conditions"), on the noun or the following relative-clause word (in, which, where, around), where a clause describing the setting is about to be introduced. Silent on "business/workplace environment" as a plain noun.
result.label: Created environment, relative clause linker

result.description: Fires on " revolution"/" Revolution", most strongly in the math phrase "solids of revolution" (also "axis of revolution"). It stays silent on "revolutions" after "circles and" and "volume revolution".
result.label: revolution in "solids of revolution"

result.description: Fires on connectives (' and', ' are', ' while', comma) right after the word "facts" or in fact-versus-opinion contrasts. It stays quiet on 'and' in ordinary lists of emotions or items.
result.label: Connectives in facts-vs-opinions text

result.description: Fires on the last piece of a field or discipline name inside a "from X to Y" or "various fields/tools" list, e.g. "Scenario Planning", "remote sensing", "computer science". Evidence is thin and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Field name endings in lists

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (' changing', ' the', 'ain' in 'sustain', ' moving', ' a') mid-phrase in abstract expository text. Members are generic token detectors with no discriminative structure; the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered mid-phrase tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on the word or word piece after a comparative "more/less/larger" in a sentence, where a "than" is likely to come next. Peak tokens vary (surface, activity, charged, bonds, luminous). Logits boost " than" and " less".
result.label: Comparative phrase awaiting "than"

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on varied mid-word or word-piece tokens (hyphens, 'syn', ' pl', ' control') where the next token is a continuation. Members are generic token detectors. The evidence is thin and unclear.
result.label: Mixed word-piece continuation positions

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on ' and' after "discovered the electron", on ' provided', and at document start. Members are scattered token detectors and the circuit failed, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Mixed ' and' / ' provided' connectives

result.description: Fires on the token " bond" when it is a stem expected to be followed by "-ing", as in "chemical bond|ing", in chemistry text. It stays silent on "double bond" as a complete noun.
result.label: chemical " bond" before -ing

result.description: Fires on the word or link right after a "The foundation of X is/lies in/built upon..." opening, such as "in", "upon", "on", "of". It needs the sentence to be about what something's foundation is. The same prepositions elsewhere stay silent.
result.label: Foundation-of statement connector words

result.description: Fires on ' and' joining two coordinated nouns after "defect detection speed" in a manufacturing/AI-improvement context. It stays silent on ' and' in many other contexts, and the cause is unclear. Members are diffuse and weak.
result.label: ' and' after "detection speed"

result.description: Fires on the function word right after "up" (scale up to/a/or/and, "up and down"), as in "scaling up" or "up and down quarks". Silent on ' and' in ordinary coordination. Members include up-hyphen detectors.
result.label: Function word after "up"

result.description: Fires on ' and' (also ' or', commas) joining two paired terms in a list of types or headings, e.g. "open-loop and closed-operator", "Credibility and Trustworthiness". Silent on many other ' and' uses. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Conjunction joining paired category terms

result.description: Fires on word-ending pieces like 'hips'/'hip' in "partnerships", and 'gy' in "synergy", in collaboration/teamwork text. It is silent on 'hips' in some contexts, so the condition is unclear. Logits point weakly to policy/national/institution words.
result.label: partnership/synergy suffix pieces

result.description: Fires on domain-noun slots (industry, world, arts, environment, domain, within) right after a field adjective like "culinary" or "business", near the start of a document, as in "In the culinary world". Silent on some later-document uses of "industry".
result.label: Field-domain noun after "In the culinary"

result.description: Fires on 'design' (and nearby 'and', 'that', '-ing') when engineers or designers are described as designing systems or processes in technical engineering text. Silent on 'design' used as a noun modifier ("design process", "design objectives"). Weakly pushes toward physics-ish tokens.
result.label: verb 'design' in engineering contexts

result.description: Fires on word pieces like "techn", "ological", "ural" right after "significant" (as in "significant technological advancements"), in historical-period text. Silent on "techn" after "as", "with", "numerous". It seems to anticipate a word continuing after "significant".
result.label: Word pieces after "significant" (technological)

result.description: Fires on the word right after "many" (mostly ' people', also plural nouns, ' but', ' and'), i.e. the noun or slot following a "many"-quantified subject. Silent on ' people' without a preceding "many". Members detect "many/various" quantifiers.
result.label: Noun after "many" quantifier

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on ' unit' in "central processing unit", plus ' complex', ' to', and 'ating'. It stays silent on 'unit' after "arithmetic/logic" and "control". Members are generic token detectors; evidence is thin.
result.label: Processing unit and scattered tokens

result.description: Fires mostly on commas and periods ending a clause or list item, plus 'forward' in "step/leap forward". Silent on many commas after introductory time phrases. Members are mostly list-comma detectors predicting 'which/including'. Circuit faithfulness is poor.
result.label: Clause-final commas and periods

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, often nouns ending a noun phrase (boundaries, reforms, team, planning) or function words like "for", in expository text. Peaks are scattered with no clear shared meaning; the circuit failed and is weak.
result.label: Scattered noun-phrase endings, unclear

result.description: Fires on " is" (also " are") right after a question-opening "What" at the start of a document, as in "What is X?". It stays silent on " is" in mid-sentence statements after a noun subject.
result.label: "is" after opening "What"

result.description: Fires on the word right after "pioneers" (' in', ' field', 'ers' of "pioneers") where a domain is about to be named, e.g. "Pioneers in the...". Silent on ' in' elsewhere, such as "change in" or "emerged in".
result.label: Pioneers in [field] slot

result.description: Fires on tokens at or just after the word "origin" (e.g. "origin of", "origin and", "origins traced", "originated"), including the "of"/"and" following it. Silent on "of" after other nouns like "development" or "flow".
result.label: Word "origin" and its continuation

result.description: Fires on ' more', ' into', ' that', ' smaller' right after "breaking/dividing a problem down into", where the next word is a smaller, simpler, manageable piece. Silent on ' more' in other constructions.
result.label: Breaking problem into smaller parts

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (" the", "1", " by", " of", "experiment") shortly after the word "experiment" in science-history text. Members mostly detect experiment/experimental words, so it seems to track nearby experiment context. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Tokens following 'experiment' in science text

result.description: Fires on commas, "),", "and", "or" inside lists or example enumerations after "such as", "including", "like". Mostly punctuation and connectors where another list item is expected. Weak, mixed evidence; silent on some commas outside lists.
result.label: Commas in example lists

result.description: Fires on " of" in the opening phrase "In today's world of" at the start of a document (essay-style intro). Silent on " of" after nouns like "integration of" or "emergence of"; weakly fires on the comma after "In today's ... landscape".
result.label: "In today's world of" opener

result.description: Fires on varied tokens that end or sit inside a noun phrase after an article or adjective (' overall', 'ive', 'de', ' experience', 'load'), often mid-word pieces. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness, so the pattern is weak.
result.label: Noun-phrase continuation, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires mostly on ' where' introducing a relative clause after a comma in physics text (e.g. "duality of forces, where one object..."), and on document-start tokens. It stays silent on other ' where' cases. The circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: ' where' after comma, physics text

result.description: Fires on ' kitchen' and nearby function words (a, of, the, your, and) in cooking/kitchen-themed text about kitchens, equipment and layout. Members include several kitchen-token detectors plus cooking-vocabulary context. Logits are unclear.
result.label: Kitchen-topic text tokens

result.description: Fires on early tokens (often ' consumer', 'anging', ' the', ' social') in a document-opening title or heading like "Changing ... consumer preferences". Silent on ' consumer' in mid-sentence prose, so it depends on being near document start.
result.label: Title-initial words in "Changing..." headings

result.description: Fires mostly on the piece 'ines' in "turbines" when it follows a steam/energy-generation context (steam that drives turb-ines). It stays silent on 'ines' in other spots, such as "Turbines" in a heading or "determines". Evidence is weak and the circuit failed.
result.label: 'ines' in turbines (steam power)

result.description: Weak, failed circuit. The target peaks on ' nuclear' (after "having enough") and on the 'ative' piece of "creative". It stays silent on ' nuclear' after "their" or "from". Members are mostly generic word-piece detectors, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: ' nuclear' after "enough", 'ative'

result.description: Fires mostly on the word " rational" (e.g. "rational decision-making", "rational actor", "rational expectation"), with a few hits on nearby "and", "," or "the". Predicts word continuations like -ity/-ism. Upstream members detect "rational" and similar word-start pieces.
result.label: word "rational" before suffix

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (' of', ' and', ' Gra', 'izable', digits, ' guests'), with low consistency. The circuit fails and its members are mixed generic detectors, so no clear trigger or condition emerges.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token attention latent

result.description: Fires on ' pione' pieces and nearby tokens (ering, like, and, E) in "pioneering work by pioneers like…" passages, where a list of pioneer names is expected. Silent on 'pione' after "early" or "this period". Evidence is mixed.
result.label: pioneer/pioneering pieces before name lists

result.description: Fires on coordinating conjunctions (" and", " or") joining items in abstract lists or phrases in explanatory prose, plus occasional " the" and "itive". Same token stays silent in many other lists, so the condition is unclear. Circuit is weak and diffuse.
result.label: Coordinating 'and'/'or' in abstract lists

result.description: Fires on 'and', 'or', commas and similar list/conjunction tokens, plus odd pieces like ' Poly' and apostrophes, mostly in lists of abstract nouns. It stays silent on many 'and' tokens, and the evidence for what separates them is unclear. The circuit failed.
result.label: List conjunctions in noun lists

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, plural 's', 'and', word pieces) inside technical science lists and terminology, such as nuclear reactors, radiation, and materials. It predicts property-type words like polar or neutral. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Science-list commas and word pieces

result.description: Weak, mixed target peaking on scattered tokens (' the' after 'increasing', 'cont' in 'oxygen-cont(aining)', 'gen' in 'oxygen-hydrogen'). Silent on ' the' elsewhere. Members are generic token detectors; the circuit failed, so evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered tokens, unclear (oxygen-cont, the)

result.description: Fires on 'and' (also commas, 'as well as') joining abstract academic nouns in social science/linguistics lists, like "culture and language" or "media, message, and society". Silent on many other 'and' tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Conjunctions in social-science noun lists

result.description: Fires on " reduction" (also "ation" in "fixation") as the second item in a list of Calvin cycle stages after "carbon fixation,". Silent on "reduction" used in other sentence positions, like "further reduction".
result.label: Calvin cycle stage list: reduction

result.description: Fires on the comma that closes an introductory participial or prepositional phrase (e.g. "Using these strategies,") right before the main clause's subject. It stays silent on list-item commas and commas that continue a series.
result.label: Comma after introductory phrase

result.description: Fires on "Common"/"common" (often in "Greatest Common Divisor/Factor") and on the token after it, such as " F" or "and". Members mostly detect " common" itself. Weaker firing appears in "common ground/risks" contexts.
result.label: "Common" and following token

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", and "including" that follow an item in a list of abstract nouns or activities (training, videos, areas), where another list item comes next. Weak, mixed circuit that failed faithfulness; silent on many commas.
result.label: List-item separators in abstract lists

result.description: Fires on commas, ' (', ' or' and similar tokens that continue a list of examples (e.g. "such as pepper, cinnamon, cloves, or"). It stays silent on commas that end a clause. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: List-continuation punctuation after examples

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' is', ' forms', ' levels', word pieces) mostly where a subject has just been stated and a verb or predicate is expected, in abstract explanatory prose. Silent on ' is' after 'it' or some subjects. Evidence is mixed and the circuit fit is poor.
result.label: Scattered subject-verb slot in essays

result.description: Fires weakly on varied function words and word pieces (' and', ' in', ' about', ' to') in academic or analytical prose. The peaks have no clear shared token, and the same ' and' stays silent in many contrast contexts. The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered function words in academic prose

result.description: Fires on coordinating tokens (' and', '/', 'wide') joining abstract nouns in broad, globalized or economic-style prose, e.g. "towns and cities", "continents and cultures". Silent on many other ' and' uses; the condition is not clear. Weak circuit.
result.label: Coordinating 'and' in abstract noun pairs

result.description: Peaks scatter across unrelated tokens (' of', digits, ' were', suffix pieces, 'create') in academic or technical prose. Silent on ' of' in other contexts. Members are generic token detectors; the circuit failed faithfulness, so evidence is weak.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository prose

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (word endings like 'el'/'ed', 'and', 'made', 'more') inside the predicate after "[Subject topic] can be/…", in abstract subject-opening sentences at document start. Members are mostly generic token detectors; evidence is mixed.
result.label: Predicate after "can be" in abstract openers

result.description: Fires on commas, "and", and list-like tokens inside enumerations of topics or items (e.g., "such as X, Y", lists of subjects or categories). Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; the circuit is a failed, diffuse one that pushes list continuation.
result.label: List separators in enumerations

result.description: Fires mostly on " collect" (as in "individual and collective") and on related individual-vs-group words (their, they, group) when a contrast between individual and collective is being set up. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: individual-and-collective contrast

result.description: Peaks scatter across mixed tokens (' to', 'ved', 'ities', ' from', ' the', ' in') in academic or expository text, often mid-word or after a word stem. Contrast shows ' to' staying silent in ordinary uses. No clear single condition is evident.
result.label: Scattered expository-text tokens, unclear

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (for, to, and, or, of, like) following a noun in product, material or business-style descriptive text, in lists or "variety of" constructions. Silent on many 'for' tokens elsewhere; the evidence is mixed and the circuit failed.
result.label: Connective words after nouns in product text

result.description: Fires on varied nouns (scenes, expressions, colors, types, pressure) that follow a modifier or verb in advice-style writing tips. Peaks are scattered and consistency is low, so the pattern is diffuse and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Object nouns in writing-advice lists

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces, often mid-word or word-final fragments (' p', 'rag', 'der', 'ics', 'ables'), and sometimes on function words. It is silent on ' p' when that begins 'pragmatics' or 'pivotal'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is a poor fit.
result.label: Scattered word-piece fragments, unclear

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered function words and punctuation (commas, 'it', 'as', 'that', 'a') in expository text, mid-clause. No coherent token or context; the circuit failed and members are generic.
result.label: Scattered function-word mid-clause latent

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly word-final or mid-phrase pieces (philos-opher, postul-ates, ' using', myth-s) in academic, abstract prose. Peaks are inconsistent and the contrast is silent on the same 'opher' token. The circuit failed and is mixed.
result.label: Scattered academic-prose word pieces

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ary' completing "integumentary" (skin-system anatomy text), with weaker firing on the following function words. It stays silent on 'ary' in other words such as evolutionary or axillary.
result.label: 'ary' in "integumentary"

result.description: Fires on ' and' (also ' or') joining items in a list of technical terms, especially the last 'and' in a list of Big O / Big Theta / Big Omega notations. It stays quiet on 'and' in other lists and clauses.
result.label: 'and' in Big O notation lists

result.description: Fires on the preposition or connector after "serves as a backdrop/canvas" (mostly ' for', also 'that', 'which', 'and'). It stays silent on some similar ' for' cases, and the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Connector after "serving as a backdrop"

result.description: Fires on the comma that closes a sentence-initial prepositional phrase such as "For many people," or "For chefs," near the start of a document. It stays quiet on commas after full clauses or mid-sentence list or relative commas.
result.label: Comma after opening 'For X' phrase
Function words in population geography text
result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (in, and, of, for, are, shape) within passages about population, density and ecology or geography. Members detect 'population' and related topic words. Silent on the same words in urban or economic text.

Fires mostly on ' perfect' in economics text about market structures, especially "perfect competition" or "perfect information". It stays silent on 'perfect' in other senses, such as Platonic forms or when it follows "and" or "with". Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: 'perfect' in economics market contexts

result.description: Fires on ' with' (also ' and', ' by') linking two abstract academic concepts, as in "intersected with", "bridging X with", "connection between X and". It is silent on other uses of ' with'. The circuit failed and its members are diffuse.
result.label: with/and linking two concepts

result.description: Fires on the "es" ending of "exercises" (and the "cis" piece in "exer-cis-es"), mostly in educational or training text. It stays silent on "es" endings of other plurals or verbs such as themes, challenges, discusses.
result.label: "exercises" word ending

result.description: Fires on a comma, "there", or "was/were" that follows an introductory phrase naming a historical period or era (e.g. "(Renaissance), there is", "the Baroque period, an"), right before the main clause. Silent after a bare "This period,". Weak evidence.
result.label: Comma after historical period phrase

result.description: Fires on ' those' right after "For" (e.g. "For those who/interested in"), usually at the start of a sentence. It is quieter after other words like "by" or "necessarily", where the target stays silent.
result.label: "For those" sentence opener

result.description: Fires on sentence-ending periods, semicolons and some function words in list-like academic or topic-heading text, plus ' Communic' in repeated headings. Silent on many periods elsewhere, so the condition is unclear. Members are mostly generic token detectors.
result.label: Periods in list-like academic text

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces like 'ist', 'ential', 'omen' inside philosophy terms such as Existentialist, Existentialism, Phenomenology. It stays silent on 'ist' in other words (epistemic, structuralist, existing-ist), so it needs the existential/phenomenological word context.
result.label: Existentialism/phenomenology word pieces

result.description: Fires mostly on " cleared" after farmers or farming communities (land clearing for agriculture), and weakly on other environment or resource-use words like "resource" and "oring". The circuit failed and is weak, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Land-clearing verb " cleared"

result.description: Fires mostly on " human" right after "juxtaposes" in text about storytelling and literary approaches, with a few other peaks (" and", " the", "igs"). Silent on " human" after "the" or "of". Members are weak and diffuse; the circuit failed.
result.label: " human" after "juxtaposes" in storytelling

result.description: Fires on word pieces mid-compound or mid-word (carbohydrate, lobe-finned, -ical, -ate), where a word is unfinished. The pattern is inconsistent and the circuit failed faithfulness; members are generic word-ending detectors.
result.label: Mid-word suffix pieces in technical terms

result.description: Weak, diffuse target firing on scattered tokens (' the', ' and' in lists, ' concerns', ' tips', ' question') with no clear pattern. Members are generic and non-discriminative; the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Diffuse function-word target, unclear

result.description: Fires on ' the' (also ' a', commas) right after a sentence-opening purpose clause like "To ensure/maintain/achieve", before an abstract quality noun (safety, stability, integrity). Silent on ' the' in other constructions.
result.label: 'the' after "To ensure"

result.description: Weak, scattered circuit that peaks on varied tokens (commas, ' one', ' America', ' than') with no clear shared context. Members are mostly word-piece and generic detectors. Evidence is thin and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token, unclear circuit

result.description: Fires on commas, "is"/"are", "that" and similar slots right after a subject noun phrase (often after "providing feedback" or a topic noun) in abstract organizational or educational prose, where a verb or clause comes next. Silent on many commas in lists.
result.label: Clause boundary after abstract subject

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on varied tokens (' the', ' and', ' on', word-final pieces like 'ures', 's') in academic or technical text, often at the end of a noun phrase or title. Peak tokens are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the evidence is thin.
result.label: Diffuse academic-text token positions

result.description: Fires on varied function and head words (of, and, the, a, system, thermal) inside statistical mechanics / thermodynamics text about ensembles, particles and systems. Members are thermodynamics and ensemble detectors; it is topic-driven rather than tied to one token.
result.label: Thermodynamics ensemble text positions
Verb/preposition after "changes in" subject
result.description: Fires on the function word right after the subject in sentences like "[Changes] in atmospheric pressure can/are/lead to...", mostly modal ' can', ' are', ' to'. Silent on ' can' in other contexts. Circuit is weak and members are generic.

Fires mostly on " is" (also "it", commas, "to") after a subject phrase like "the driving force/central idea/principle behind X", where the predicate is about to be stated. Members are diffuse and the circuit is weak.
result.label: 'is' after "behind X" subject phrase

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (' to', ' and', ' for', ' that', ' specific') in abstract expository lists and prose. The contrast shows it is silent on many ' to' tokens, and the evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on mid-sentence connectives (' and', ' to') and word-piece endings (ives, ins, ury) in lists of academic or expository text. Silent on 'and' closing a simple list of nouns. Evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Mid-clause 'and' and word pieces

result.description: Weak, mixed target firing on sentence-ending periods in literary or academic summaries, plus pieces like 'ological', ' era', ' quantum'. Contrast shows the same '.' staying silent, and members are mostly generic token detectors. Evidence is thin.
result.label: Periods in literary/academic summaries (unclear)

result.description: Fires on evaluative adjectives like "significant", "important", "practical" (also "to", "innovative") in text about technological or scientific advances and breakthroughs, just before a noun like impact or improvements. It stays silent on "significant" in some historical-progress phrasings, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Significance adjectives before advancement nouns

result.description: Fires mostly on " water" (also environmental, structures, management) right after "X and" in a "flood control and water resource management" phrase. Silent on " water" in other constructions, so the "and"-coordination slot seems to matter. Weak circuit.
result.label: "and water" in resource-management coordination

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in expository text (function words like 'and', 'a', 'to', 'from', plus noun and word-piece endings) where a noun phrase or term could continue. Weak, mixed evidence; the circuit failed faithfulness and the members are diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase tokens in expository text

result.description: Fires mostly on ' an' in "your community as an orchestra" (metaphor framing), plus odd pieces like ' Sym' in "Symphony". Silent on ' an' elsewhere. Circuit failed faithfulness and members are diffuse, so the evidence is weak.
result.label: ' an' in "as an orchestra" metaphor

result.description: Fires on connectives (' and', ',', ' with') right after "sustainable/sustainability" phrases, e.g. "sustainable design principles and". Silent on 'and' in other lists or contexts, so it needs a sustainability topic. Evidence is weak and mixed.
result.label: 'and' after sustainability phrases

result.description: Fires on commas, "such as", "within" or "ors" right after "receptors" (also "factors") in biology text, where a list or elaboration follows. Silent on commas after other biology nouns like "growth factors".
result.label: Punctuation after "receptors" in biology

result.description: Fires on mixed function tokens (commas, 'and', 'of', 'the') inside lists of items or technical, scientific enumerations, with a weak, scattered pattern. Members mostly detect list items and listing words; evidence is thin and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Function tokens within technical lists

result.description: Fires on function words (is, of, a, just, aspect) in essays about listening and communication, mid-sentence after a listening/communication subject. Silent on 'is' in other topics, so it depends on the listening theme.
result.label: Function words in listening essays

result.description: Weak, mixed attention-layer target peaking on scattered words (' balance', ' suggest', ' are', ' or', ' communication') in abstract essay-like prose, often after a comma or in a list. Members are generic token detectors; evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered abstract-prose words (balance, suggest)

result.description: Fires on varied mid-phrase tokens (' and', ' up', ' objects', ' stages', ' or', ' flows') in abstract academic/technical prose, often after a noun modifier; peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak. Predicts verbs like develop/existing/learning.
result.label: Mixed mid-phrase tokens in technical prose

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly commas, "and", "that" within lists or noun series in academic or scientific text (anatomy, geography, policy). The peaks are inconsistent and the circuit failed, so the pattern is weak and unclear.
result.label: Commas and conjunctions in academic lists

result.description: Fires on words in biology/variation passages (e.g. "variation", "to", "from", "which") where a genetic-variation concept is being discussed or continued. It is silent on some "variation" tokens in survival and selection contexts, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: genetic variation discussion words

result.description: Fires on the word piece "het" in "rhetoric"/"rhetorical" right after "r", completing the word. It is weaker on "or" in "Rhetoric" and on "m" in "Pragmatic". Members detect "r"+"het" and related word pieces.
result.label: "het" inside "rhetoric"

result.description: Fires on the noun after "building" in "fundamental building block(s)", and weakly on similar nouns like "key drivers" or "heroes". Members detect foundation/block/hub words in "the basis of X" phrasing.
result.label: building blocks / foundation nouns

result.description: Fires at the end of an item in a list of abstract nouns or business and technical terms (commas, 'and', word-ending pieces like -ency, -iveness), where the list continues. Silent on some commas in scientific lists. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: List-item boundaries in abstract noun lists

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'en' inside 'millennium' (mill-en-nium), peaking at the turn-of-the-millennium phrase. Members mostly detect 'en' in other words (Zen, Enlightenment), but the target is silent on unrelated text.
result.label: 'en' in millennium

result.description: Fires on " of" right after "phase"/"stage" in process-description text (e.g. "final phase of the...", "last stage of developmental..."). It stays silent on "of" after other nouns like "every stage of" or "part of", so it is selective.
result.label: "of" after final phase/stage

result.description: Fires on " I" in the quoted Descartes phrase "I think, therefore I am", the " I" right after "therefore". Weak activation on words after "think" in casual speech. Silent on a bare "Cogito" mention.
result.label: "therefore I am" — I

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (mid-word pieces, 'and', commas, nouns after adjectives) in abstract academic-style prose, mostly where a noun phrase or word is incomplete or continues. Peaks are scattered and the circuit is weak and diffuse, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in abstract prose

result.description: Fires mainly on " engaged" (especially "keep readers engaged"), and occasionally on "th" in Carthage or similar word pieces. Members detect engage/engaged/engagement forms. It stays silent on "emotionally connected" phrasing.
result.label: "engaged" after keep readers

result.description: Fires on word-initial fragments of multi-piece words, such as 'Hus' in Husserl, 'amb' in gambling, and 'cor' in underscoring or incorporating. It predicts a continuation piece and is silent when 'Hus' starts the document.
result.label: Incomplete word-start fragments (Hus, cor, amb)

result.description: Fires mostly on " the" (also "of", "ional") after "the rhythm/pace/tempo of" in writing-pacing text, before "narrative/story". Members detect pace/tempo/narrative words. Silent on " the" after "aspects of" in other contexts.
result.label: "the" after pace/rhythm of (narrative)

result.description: Fires on ' including' introducing a list of examples or subgroups after a general noun phrase (e.g. "everyone, including individuals with..."). Members detect include/including/such as. Silent in at least one financial-analysis "including" case.
result.label: ' including' introducing example subgroups

result.description: Fires mostly on ' AV' in "AVL Trees", plus scattered word pieces like 'ass', 'se(ek)', 'ival' inside longer words. Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is only partly clear.
result.label: AV in AVL Trees, word pieces

result.description: Fires mostly on " quest" in "the quest for X" (search/seeking-for nouns), with scattered weaker hits on other tokens. Members detect search/query/necessity words that precede "for". Circuit is weak and mixed.
result.label: "quest" in "quest for"

result.description: Fires on prepositions (" of", " from", " in") after a noun in abstract descriptive prose, where a noun complement follows. Silent on many other " of" uses (e.g. "layers of", "capable of", "face of"). Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Prepositions after nouns (of/from/in)

result.description: Peaks scatter across unrelated tokens (' for', ' traces', ' starting', ' through', word pieces) in expository history/academic text. No consistent token or context; the circuit failed and members are generic.
result.label: Scattered mixed-token target, unclear

result.description: Fires on "aring" in "wearing" (split as we|aring) and on " wear" as a verb, mostly with clothing context. Members detect the wear/aring pieces. Weak activation on a few stray tokens.
result.label: "wearing" / "wear" word pieces

result.description: Fires on the start of a new topic-title line in lists of academic subject headings (e.g. " Cultural" after a line break, "International", "lingu-istic"), often the first word of a term in a list of course or topic names. Mixed and weak evidence.
result.label: List-item topic title words (Cultural, International)

result.description: Fires on ' a'/' an' (also 'mere', 'supp') right after a "not only/just/merely/more than just" negated-restriction phrase, where a contrasting "but" clause is expected. Silent on ordinary ' a' after verbs or prepositions.
result.label: article after "more than just/merely"

result.description: Fires on the word piece "inter" when it follows the prefix "re" (as in "reinterpreted"). Members detect prefix pieces like inter, im, def and product after "re". The target is silent on "intersect" in the contrast.
result.label: "inter" after re- prefix

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'on' in "harm-on-ious/harmonize" and on 'oust' in "ac-oust-ic", mid-word pieces in sound/music/design text. Weakly on 'compos' in "compositions". Predicts suffixes like -ious or -ic.
result.label: Mid-word 'on' in harmonious, 'oust' in acoustic

result.description: Fires on the word piece "vit" (starting "vitamin") in nutrition and food text, and on "it" inside words like "gravitational". Members detect vit/Vit, nut-, and food-source words.
result.label: vit- piece in vitamin

result.description: Fires on the word-piece 'am' inside longer words like seamlessly, ceramic, creaminess, among, and on ' Ch' in "Supply Chain" at document start. Silent on 'am' in "Examining". Mostly a mid-word fragment detector, with a weak logit push toward suffixes like -lessly.
result.label: 'am' mid-word fragment (se-am-lessly)

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'in' inside "ref-in-ement/ery" (and ' cam' in camera words), a mid-word fragment where a suffix like -ement or -ery follows. Silent on 'in' in prominence, Ruin, Einstein.
result.label: Mid-word 'in' in refinement

result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece "raction" in refraction/diffraction, in optics and physics text. It is silent when "raction" starts a document with no "ref" or "diff" before it. Weak activation on a few other word pieces and "of".
result.label: "raction" in refraction/diffraction

result.description: Fires on ' well' as the start of a word or compound (well-being, well-defined, wells) and on word pieces like 'law' in flawless, 'exception'. Silent on 'as well as'. Predicts word-continuation suffixes.
result.label: 'well' prefix in compounds, not 'as well as'
Mid-word pieces in medical therapy terms
result.description: Fires on word-internal pieces (onal, ap, ine, ics, ant) inside multi-token medical/biomedical words, such as monocl-onal, Ther-ap-ies, radi-other-apy, in therapy and treatment text. Members are medical-context detectors predicting a continuation of the word.

Fires on ' work' (also book, paper) as a noun naming a scholar's authored output, especially after "seminal", "pioneering" or a possessive in academic biographical text. Silent on 'work' in other senses or slots.
result.label: Seminal work noun after praise adjective

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'ament' piece in "testament" (as in "a testament to"), with weak scattered activation on other word pieces, Arabic endings and zero-width characters. Members detect the "test" prefix and the "ament" piece.
result.label: 'ament' in "testament"

result.description: Fires on the word-start fragment ' spons' (sponsorship) and on 'och' in 'mitochondrial', i.e. incomplete word pieces that need a continuation. Silent on the contrast text, which has no such fragment.
result.label: spons / och word-piece fragments

result.description: Fires on the apostrophe in possessive 's after a noun (e.g. "biology's", "Theme's") at the start of abstract academic-style text, and on the "estr" piece of "orchestrates/orchestration". Silent on apostrophes after pronouns or in quotes.
result.label: Possessive apostrophe and orchestr- piece

result.description: Fires on mid-word or word-ending pieces (counter-part, semiconduct-or, p-type, microb-ial, ' pro') in science text, where the word may continue or complete. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak; silent on ' pro' in proton words.
result.label: Word-piece fragments in technical text

result.description: Fires mainly on 'ent' in "underwent" and 'one' in "undergone", the "undergo" forms, plus scattered tokens like " finished" and " many". Silent on 'ent' in unrelated words such as turbulent or nutrient.
result.label: undergo forms (underwent/undergone)

result.description: Fires mainly on " close" as an adjective after "paying/pay" or a determiner, as in "paying close attention" or "close relationships". Members detect close/closer/closed. Weaker on a few word pieces like "ance".
result.label: "close" in "paying close attention"

result.description: Fires on the word " without" when it follows a verb phrase or clause and introduces a manner or exclusion ("transfer X without losing..."). It stays quiet after "even" at the start of a phrase. Members are mostly " without" detectors from earlier layers.
result.label: " without" after a clause

result.description: Fires on word-start fragments ' eth' (before "ics", as in medical eth-ics, virtue eth-ics) and ' sc' (sc-anners, sc-affold) that begin a split word. It is silent on ' eth' before "ical" in other contexts, so it depends on the word being completed.
result.label: ' eth' / ' sc' word-start fragments

result.description: Fires on the standalone token 'n', mostly as a math variable (n+1, n!, a_n, choosing n items), and also inside words like supernova. Weaker on ' group' and 'N'. Silent on 'n' as a subscript in C_n(X).
result.label: Letter 'n' as math variable

result.description: Fires on "when" (or "When") introducing a subordinate clause, often after a semicolon, colon, "that", or at sentence start. It stays quiet when "when" follows a noun, as in "moments when" or "pleasure when".
result.label: Clause-introducing "when"

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and word pieces (' of', ' to', ' an', ' its', 'ous') in abstract, philosophical or academic explanatory prose. It is silent on many ' of' tokens after abstract nouns, so the evidence is mixed and the trigger is not clear.
result.label: Scattered function words in abstract prose

result.description: Fires on varied tokens, mostly the first word piece of a new list item or heading line (' Pr' in "Pronoun", ' Ad' in "Adverbs") and occasionally mid-sentence words like 'environmental' or 'un'. Evidence is mixed; the logits show no clear next-token pattern.
result.label: List-item initial word pieces (Pr, Ad)

result.description: Fires on auxiliary "have/had/has" (and would/will have) in discussion of perfect tenses and verb conjugation, where a participle like "been" is expected next. Silent on "have" in relative clauses ("which have", "that have").
result.label: Perfect-tense auxiliary have/had

result.description: Fires on the word "festival"/"Festival" (and variants) in text about events, such as "Music Festival" headings or "festival attendance". Members are mostly festival and event-word detectors. It stays silent on one quoted instance, but the evidence for why is thin.
result.label: festival token detector

result.description: Fires mostly on the 'st' piece in "overstated"/"overstating" (after "over"), i.e. a mid-word fragment awaiting a suffix. Silent on ordinal "21st". Weak firing on other word-start fragments and odd tokens.
result.label: 'st' inside "over-stated"

result.description: Fires on varied tokens in phrases about what was not possible or not done before ("previously unimagined", "never before seen", "words alone could not", "can compete"), where a modal or adverb precedes a verb. Mixed, low consistency.
result.label: Previously/could capability phrasing

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, mostly ' they', ' closer', ' will' and word pieces, in explanatory academic/economic prose where a subject is about to take a verb or comparison. Silent on many ' they' in other clauses. Evidence is mixed and weak.
result.label: Scattered ' they' in explanatory prose
search / searching word detector
result.description: Fires on the words "search" and "searching" (also "retrieve"), mostly in computing and information-retrieval text about search algorithms or indexing. It stays silent on "search" in compound names like "grid search" and "binary search trees".

Fires on "ender" in "Gender" and on " gender", strongest in repeated "Gender and X" headings at document start. Silent on "ender" in mid-sentence "Gender stereotypes" and in a fragmentary "ender roles" context.
result.label: Gender token in headings

result.description: Fires on " is" right after a short abstract noun-phrase subject that opens a general statement, especially business/management concepts at sentence start ("Succession planning is…"). Silent on "is" after pronouns, or after longer subjects mid-sentence.
result.label: " is" after abstract concept subject

result.description: Fires on ' for' right after a subject noun and comma, opening an illustrative aside ("X, for example/instance"). It stays silent on ' for' as an ordinary preposition (formula for, crucial for). It predicts ' example'/' instance'.
result.label: ", for example" aside opener

result.description: Fires on a mid-word piece, mostly 'ation' in "Penetration" (also 'and' in "merchandise"), when it completes a specific word after a split-word prefix. Silent on 'ation' in revelation, experimentation, innovation.
result.label: Penetration 'ation' word-piece

result.description: Fires weakly on scattered function words and word pieces (' in', ' or', ' and', ' within', ' spin') inside abstract science or social-science expository text, often mid-phrase. No clear single trigger; the circuit failed and members are diffuse.
result.label: Scattered connectives in abstract expository text

result.description: Fires on abstract process/project nouns in professional or engineering lists (development, design, campaign, construct, activity), often within lists of tasks. Silent on one 'development' example. Members are mostly generic word-piece detectors, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Project/process nouns in lists

result.description: Fires on "royal" and the "ty" in "royalty" (payments for use of music or IP, and also royal/noble contexts). Members detect " royal", "noble" and "ty" tokens. Silent on nearby text about music earnings without the word.
result.label: royal / royalty token

result.description: Fires on 'and', 'or' or a comma right after an adjective like "subtle", "nuanced" or "intricate", where another adjective is expected next. It stays silent on 'and' after nouns or other adjectives. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Conjunction after 'subtle' adjective

result.description: Fires on the 'LC' of the acronym SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle) when it is introduced in parentheses, and on 'Cy' in 'Life Cycle'. Also weakly on mid-word fragments. Silent on later 'SDLC' uses in running text.
result.label: SDLC acronym 'LC' piece

result.description: Fires on " transformations" (also " transformation", "maps", "mappings") mainly in linear algebra or math text, such as "linear transformations". It is silent on other math text that lacks the word, like vector spaces and dimension.
result.label: "transformations" in math text

result.description: Fires on incomplete first word-pieces in the middle of a multi-token word, such as ' er' (erosion), ' pros' (prosody), and 'ain' (Remainder). It expects a continuation piece to complete the word.
result.label: Mid-word fragment awaiting completion

result.description: Fires on ' data' (also datasets, information) as the noun ending a phrase like "large amounts of data" or "vast datasets", in big-data/analytics text. Silent when data begins a phrase or is a subject, e.g. "data analytics", "As data expands".
result.label: data after quantity/modifier phrase

result.description: Fires on pieces of "sophisticated"-like words (s, istic, ated) or a preceding adverb, when the text describes a shift from simple or rudimentary systems to something more advanced. Silent on "more sophisticated" without that contrast.
result.label: Simple-to-sophisticated shift, word pieces

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' mus' (as in muscle, muscular, musician), mostly in anatomy text about muscle types. Members are mostly ' mus' token detectors; the logits favour continuations like 'cle', 'cles' and 'icians'.
result.label: ' mus' word-start piece (muscle)

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens (commas, 'of', 'technique', word-piece endings, 'ly') in expository lists and technical prose. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low; it stays silent on many commas in similar lists, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Scattered tokens in expository lists

result.description: Fires on a mix of tokens: ' entropy', ' N' at the start of a heading line (Nouns, Nuclear), ' only', and ' or'. The peaks share no single meaning and the circuit is diffuse, so the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Entropy, heading-initial N, only

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' staff', ' and', ' come', commas) in abstract expository text about people, groups, cultures and organizations, often right after a coordinated list. Peaks are inconsistent and ' staff' stays silent in some contexts; the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Scattered tokens in list-like organizational prose

result.description: Fires on a scattering of tokens: digits inside numbers (e.g. '9' in 299.79, 1899), plus function words like ' the', ' in', ' above', ' for'. Logits favor plural abstract nouns (areas, changes, data). No clear single trigger; the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse digits and function words

result.description: Fires on incomplete word pieces in the middle of a multi-token word or name (Mic-row-wave, Mac-intosh, Carl, Fact-ors), where the next piece completes the word. Silent on 'row' in an unrelated name (Drowne).
result.label: Mid-word piece before completion
